The frame is clearly darker than the reference, so it is not clearly better: the board below the card and the case's left edge sink into the dark navy wall, the KORRIN Z7 chipset plate that reads in the reference is lost, and the desk is a black void with only a few colored blips of reflection at the bottom and no contact shading under the case.

This is darker than the reference and not clearly better: the lower half of the board under the card is murky, the card's fin opening under the light bar is solid black, and the case floor, feet and base merge into a pure black desk that reflects only the front fan rings and not the case body.

The left half of the frame is a black void that swallows the case's rear edge, top and base, and the desk shows no surface and only a faint reflection, so the readable desk edge and grounded reflection of the reference are gone and this is not clearly better.

The new top I/O and shroud grommet are gains, but the case's front face and lower body fade into a black desk with no contact shading and only the fan rings reflected below, and the board behind the card is unreadable, so the frame reads darker and less grounded than the reference.

The rear I/O, fan grille, slot covers and supply switch are a real gain over the reference, but the right half of the frame is pure black, so the case's front edge, top right corner and base melt away, and the desk shows no contact shading and no reflection of the case body.

Under the softboxes alone the front mesh face at right and the board below the card fall almost to black, and the case stands on a desk that reads as a black void with no visible contact shading and no reflection of the body, with only the feet suggesting a floor.

The fin stack under the light bar is a solid black slot where the reference showed real fins, a broad white glass reflection band washes over the left third of the card, and the cyan to magenta bar throws no visible light onto the sleeved cable that crosses it or onto the shroud face below it.

The pump head sits against the board with no visible mounting bracket or screws (the reference showed its bracket), the bright cyan pump ring leaves the M.2 plate and board around it unlit, and the rear fan's blades at top left have ragged, torn-looking edges.

The Facet sticks read as flat black slabs with no faceting and no notched top line, their lit bars throw no color onto the spreaders or the board beside them, and the two pump tubes rise from their fittings and merge into one run along the top.

The card's fin stack across the top third is a black void and the board below is so dim its traces barely read, a thin black lead runs dead straight through the air from the board's right edge out of frame at mid height with no tie or support, and a broad glass reflection band washes the left fifth, so this is not clearly better than the reference.

Behind the mesh the three front fans are almost black, showing only a dim ring and faint blades, and their frames, corner pads, struts and hub sticker cannot be read, while the reference shows blades and rings more clearly, so this is not better than the floor.

Two broad white glass reflection bands cut diagonally across the frame and wash the 24 pin bundle and the memory toward grey, and a thin black lead from the bottom of the pump curls down and disappears into the M.2 heatsink plate.

The frame is so underexposed that the case rear, the supply plate edges and the case's lower edge fade into navy black, the large rear panel is one flat fill with no variation, and the power inlet is a flat plug glyph printed in a square instead of a recessed three pin inlet.

Under the lid and label, the Vault drive body is a plain dark box with no cast form or side screw holes, the shroud face and the empty lower bay are flat black fills with no variation, and the grid text on the label shows only as grey smudged dashes.

The glass mid tower reads at once, and I found no fail item: the glass has a border, corner fixings and a reflection, the front is fine round perforation, and the tray grommets, standoffs, slot wall, rear fan grille, connector cutout, vented shroud with its brand plate, drive cage, top ports and feet are all present.

The back is finished, with rounded edges and a fine grain on the solid side panel, and the rear panel shows the fan grille, connector cutout, vented slot covers with their screw strip, the supply opening, a thumbscrew and feet, all readable against the dark background.

Up close the glass shows a painted border, a visible edge and a reflection, the corner fixing cap and rounded frame pillar catch light, and the top and front perforation is crisp with no moire, alongside the front port panel and the tray grommet and standoffs.
The magenta accent on the right edge of the chipset plate and the blue strip on the connector cover glow as thin lines but put no colored light on the plate, the cover or the board around them.

The back shows solder rows, mounting rings and a plain backplate but no screw heads or nuts under the voltage regulator heatsinks or the chipset heatsink, so those front pieces have no visible fastening anywhere on the board.
The opening inside the socket's retention frame is a flat black square with no contact field and no cap detail, and the inner bottom left corner of the frame throws a white pinpoint sparkle.

The heat spreader top, which fills most of the frame, is a smooth gradient with no grain, lapping or roughness variation, and the green substrate is an even green fill, so the nickel reads as a computer generated surface.
The underside shows a dense gold pad field with no moire, a center patch of components, the gold corner triangle and a visible green substrate edge, so it is finished and reads as a processor.

At the closest view the heat spreader top is a smooth, even gradient with no grain or lapping texture, and the substrate is a flat green fill with no trace or solder mask variation, so the surfaces fail the lean in test even though the etched text is sharp.

The fan rings tint their own blades, but the cyan pump ring puts no light on the pump face, fittings or the turntable under it, the turntable below the radiator stays dark, and the tubes carry a smooth unbroken highlight that reads as rubber hose, not braid.

The radiator core reads as plain horizontal slats with no corrugated fins between the tubes, the left end tank and lower body sink into the black backdrop, the small print on the top rail near the right tank is an unreadable smear, and three fan leads stick stiffly straight up into the air above the top edge.

The Gale Lux blades read as solid navy plastic, not smoked translucent, the tube sleeving reads as a dimpled rubber grip and not woven braid, and the pump's two lit rings throw none of their color onto the black pump face or the nearby fan blades.

The cyan middle of the light bar washes out to near white, the bar puts no colored light on the spreader lip and facets just below it, and the gold contact fingers on the right half have a ragged uneven top edge that reads as aliasing.

Faint ghost letters of the CALYRA wordmark show through along the top edge of the spec label, the cyan section of the bar fades to near white, the bar does not tint the spreader beneath it, and the contact fingers have a ragged top edge.

At this close view the gold contact fingers are uneven heights like a jagged waveform and not a clean even row of pads, the left end of the light bar clips to near white, and the strong pink run puts no color on the brushed spreader lip right under it.

The far right end of the card is capped by a plain flat slab that stands taller than the chamfered shroud and apart from it, the fan face is a flat plate with three round holes and not a sculpted aerodynamic shroud, and the light bar on the top edge leaves the top surfaces beside it dark.

The backplate reads as a smooth, even blue grey sheet with no brushed grain, the cutout at right shows only a flat dark fill with nothing behind it, and the end of the card is a plain rectangular slab that hangs below the card body.
The fan blade edges at bottom left and bottom right are stair stepped and toothed, and the top face around the light bar has a coarse grey mottled grain that reads as concrete, not a molded shroud.
Apart from the label, the board is a featureless black plate with no chips, components, traces or pads at either end, so the stick reads as a flat slab with a sticker and not a bare board with chips.

The underside reads as a brushed metal plate and not a circuit board, with no traces or components beyond five pads, and a clipped pure white sliver runs along the near lower edge from the screw notch to mid length like a stray strip poking out.

At the closest view the bare board by the connector is plain black with no components, traces or pads, and the label slab hides any chip shape, so the part misses the bare board with chips minimum even though the label text is sharp.
The cast body sides are a plain smooth dark box with no mounting holes, ribs or casting detail, and the fine print in the label table and under the motor circle is a grey smear.

The cast body reads as a plain smooth slab with no threaded side mounting holes and no casting form, only a flat gradient along the long side wall, and the SATA connectors at the far end are featureless black blocks with no pin slots.

A hard horizontal seam about halfway down the frame, where the cover surface overlaps the label, cuts the label off and clips the bottom spec lines on the right (256 MB CACH, 12 V 0.5 A), and the spec grid repeats the same eight lines in three columns with text sitting across its rule lines.
The honeycomb grille on top shows only pure black holes with no fan blades or hub behind it, so the visible fan that every Thessic supply must have is lost in black.
The top honeycomb grille and the rear honeycomb vent beside the inlet both show only black voids with no fan visible behind them, so the required visible fan does not read.

At the closest zoom the inset socket panel is a flat uniform black with no finish variation, and every socket cell is an empty square hole with no terminals or keying, including a 12V-2X6 socket with no sense pins, so the panel does not hold up.

The ring's top and bottom arcs wash out to pale, nearly white cyan, the black frame face right beside the ring gets no colored spill, hard-edged blue patches show inside the duct at the lower left, and the lead rises stiffly off the frame top into the image's top edge as a bare stub.

The cyan arc of the ring at the top right is pastel to nearly white, the frame face next to the ring gets no light from it, and the lead sticks straight up from the top right corner and ends in a bare cut stub with no connector.

At the closest zoom the blades read as flat, untwisted violet sheets with no visible edge thickness and smooth, unvaried surfaces, so they do not hold up as molded smoked translucent blades, even though the hub text is sharp.

The LEDs are correctly near the bottom of the breath, but the far edge of the perforated front panel at the upper right shows the same column of aliased moire, and the desk and the case base melt into black with no readable desk surface or feet.

The radiator label along the top edge reads backwards, and the three front fans glow much dimmer and muddier through the mesh than in the reference while the shroud top and the backplate wash out to pale lavender grey, so the frame is not clearly better than the reference.

The power inlet is a plain rectangular hole holding thin, hollow, bracket-shaped pins, with the left and right pins mirror images of each other, where a real inlet has a keyed recess and three parallel solid blades, and below the supply plate the case base and feet sink into black so you cannot see how the case stands on the desk.

Seen through the shroud window, the drive reads at once as a brushed metal lid with a crisp, legible paper label, barcode, spindle dome, cover screw and breather hole, the window lip has thickness and rounded corners, and the fan light grading across the lid is believable.

The plain steel right panel is calm and fits the Mirevale archetype, and the rear face shows the connector cutout, the screwed fan grille, seven vented slot covers with their retention bar, an open supply bay, the perforated top and the feet, with rolled edges catching light and nothing left unfinished.

Up close the corner shows a rounded frame rail catching light, a glossy corner standoff, a dark border band on the glass with a green-tinted glass edge and a soft reflection, a rubber grommet seen through the glass, and clean staggered round perforation on the front panel.

Clearly better than the reference: the fine round perforation shows the three lit fans with no moire, the fan light reaches the desk, and the case edge stays readable against the black left half of the room; the two thin glass streak lines across the GPU and shroud are the only flaw I found.

Clearly better than the reference, whose light bars were clipped pink white: the two sticks have saturated blue and purple bars with the notched top line, sharp CALYRA FACET and DDR5 16 GB print, and the braided tubes and combed 24 pin pass the sticks without touching them.

Clearly better than the reference's loose diagonal swoop: the 24 pin leaves straight, holds even braided black and purple wires in two combs and turns cleanly into the rubber grommet, and the EPS and GPU runs bend smoothly into their plugs.

The VELTRIN print on the backplate under the memory, center of the frame, reads upside down and mirrored from the glass side, even though the sleeved 24 pin with two combs into the rubber grommet, the processor cable and the card power plug are otherwise clearly better than the reference.

Clearly better than the reference, because the glass now reads by its corner standoffs, border and a reflection band, the shroud carries a vent field, plate and drive bay, braided tubes and combed purple cables are seated, the lit fans tint the mesh and the desk, and the case is grounded with a mirror reflection and no wall shadow.

Clearly better than the reference, because the glass reads by its edge and reflection, the braided tubes rise from the pump and run under the three lit radiator fans without touching them, the three front fans and the rear fan are lit and spill onto their surroundings, and the case stands on its feet with a clean desk reflection.

Clearly better than the reference, because the round perforated front shows three gale-lux fans with readable blades and hubs that tint the mesh purple, the side glass carries a reflection, the silhouette holds against the lit wall, and there is no moire, flare or hard wall shadow.

Clearly better than the reference, because the perforated top, the top I/O with its power button, the Vault 4 TB drive with a sharp label in its shroud bay, and the brushed backplate with its vents, cutout and exposed heat pipes all read, with nothing floating or intersecting.

Clearly better than the reference, because the rear now has an I/O cover with ports and gold antenna jacks, a grilled exhaust fan that lights its surround blue, vented slot covers with a retention bar, and a supply face with honeycomb, inlet and switch, all grounded on the desk.

With the power off the diffusers are dark as intended, and the softbox light still shows every part from the Tarn 360 Lux radiator print to the shroud vents, plate and drive bay, with nothing lost in black and the case grounded with a desk reflection.

The card itself is clearly better than the reference (brushed backplate with an X bracket and screws, slanted vents, a fin cutout, and a lit wordmark apart from the bar), but the Kestrane pump head at top center sits on the board with no mounting bracket, arms or screws visible anywhere around it.

The pump head in the center is a bare cylinder against the board with no retention bracket, arms or screws at any corner, where the reference showed a square bracket with hex screws, so even with the sharper print, braided tubes and chrome-ringed fittings it is not clearly better than the reference.

The two Facet sticks with their sharp Calyra and DDR5 16 GB print and saturated bars beat the reference, but the pump head at left center still stands against the board with no bracket or screws holding it.

Clearly better than the reference, because the lower board shows traces, the M.2_3 plate with its screw, a coin cell, pinned headers, sharp small print and mounting screws, the K chipset accent lights the board around it, and the combed card cable drops cleanly into a rounded shroud cutout.

Clearly better than the reference, because clean round perforation with no moire replaces the stretched holes, the gale-lux rings stay colored and tint the blades and mesh around them, the blades and hub read through the mesh, and mount screws sit at the fan corners.

The combed, braided 24 pin run into the rubber grommet and the card cable plug are clearly better than the reference, but the large pump head at left center has no bracket or screws holding it to the board.

The case rear panel above and to the right of the supply has a coarse blotchy noise pattern that looks like stains, not powder coat, and the honeycomb holes along the grille's right and upper right edge are cut off into partial cells.

The Vault sits recessed under a thick rounded shroud window with occlusion at the rim, the brushed cover, spindle boss, screw and breather hole read as metal, the label text and corner tab are sharp and match the catalog, and the purple interior light falls across the cover.

Every listed board feature is present and countable (4 latched memory slots, 3 M.2 plates, reinforced slot, socket frame, finned VRM heatsinks, 24 pin and processor power, coin cell, screws), and both light zones are saturated and spill onto the board beside them.

A flat, featureless, glowing pink slab sticks out past the board's far left edge at lower left and matches nothing on the front view's edge, so it looks like the chipset accent's glow leaking around the board rather than a modeled part.

The two-tier nickel spreader has beveled edges that catch the light, the etched vane mark and the model and spec lines match the catalog, and the green substrate with its visible edge, small components and gold corner triangle all read clearly.

At the close angle the etched wordmark, model line and data matrix stay sharp, the spreader shows fine grain with rounded edges that catch the light, and the substrate edge, components and corner mark hold up.

The faceted graphite spreader has the notched top line, the full length light bar tints the spreader below it, the CALYRA and DDR5 16 GB marks are sharp, and the PCB strip and keyed gold contacts match the Facet row.
The back is finished, with a sharp label giving 16 GB DDR5 and 2 x 16 GB, a matching facet, the lit bar spilling color onto the spreader and the keyed gold edge, all in line with the catalog.

Close in, the notch has smooth curves, the diffuser's front face holds saturated cyan, violet and magenta, the brushed facets catch the light on their beveled edges, and the seam between bar and spreader is clean.

Three fans with swept blades and VELTRIN hub stickers, a chamfered shroud end, and a slim gradient light bar with a lit wordmark and the 12V-2x6 socket on the glass edge all read clearly, and the bar tints the fins beneath it.

The brushed backplate has a sharp VELTRIN APEX 3X mark, slanted vents, a cutout onto the fins and heat pipes, and screws, the gold edge connector and PCB are exposed, and the light bar throws color onto the turntable below.
At the closest angle the rim edges catch the light, the recessed 12V-2x6 socket shows its pins, the bar above tints the real fin stack blue to pink, and the bar stays saturated without clipping.

The 3.5 inch drive reads at once: a brushed lid held by Phillips screws, stamped platter arcs and a breather hole, a Pellam Vault 4 TB grid label with its yellow corner tab, and a satin black body with rounded edges and three threaded side holes, and nothing on the fail list shows.

Outside the green board the underside is a flat black slab with none of the threaded bottom mounting holes a 3.5 inch drive has, and the spindle motor base at lower left reads as a glossy black rubber washer instead of a metal plate.

The label text, barcode, screws and brushing hold up, but the spindle area at lower left reads as a milky see-through disc laid over the brushed lid, with brush lines showing through its soft edge and no pressed rim, highlight or shadow, so it does not read as stamped metal.

Colors run from magenta violet at the rear fan and pump, through blue on the memory, to cyan on the front fans, and along the card bar from rear to front, which matches gradient(pn x 0.66) on the Aurora stops, and the saturated diffusers light the shroud end, the desk and the wall.

The frame is at the dim low point of the breath as defined, but the VELTRIN wordmark on the card edge facing the glass is gone into the black shroud while the thin bar above it still shows, so the wordmark has no unlit letters and the card loses its brand mark.

Every zone shows the same saturated yellow green, which matches hue fract(0.12 tau) at speed 60, and the green spills onto the card backplate, the shroud end, the desk and the wall with no clipping or flare.

The colors move through the rig as one, with a blue rear fan, cyan pump, pink memory, a card bar going from cyan at the bracket to pink at the far end, and magenta front and top fans, which matches gradient(0.8 pn minus 0.35 tau), and the saturated diffusers light the shroud, desk and wall.

Every LED holds one violet between the magenta and violet stops, which is what gradient(0.1 tau) gives at this frame, and that violet stays saturated and lights the shroud end, the desk and the wall with no haze or flare.

Each zone has a comet head as defined, but the unlit letters of the VELTRIN wordmark on the card edge disappear into the black shroud, so the card reads only IN in pink and the wordmark has no visible diffuser when its LEDs are low.

The scattered colored sparks on the fans, memory and card bar fit the starlight definition, but the VELTRIN wordmark on the card edge is lost in the black shroud with no unlit letters left, so the card's brand mark cannot be read.

At load 0 every zone is a saturated blue near hueCold, with the card bar slightly more cyan for its warmer simulated temperature, which matches the thermal mapping, and the blue lights the shroud end, the desk and the wall cleanly.

The rig stands out from the lit wall even at thumbnail size, the glass reads as glass through its painted border, corner standoffs and strip reflections, the seven lit fans, pump, memory and card bar spill color onto the parts and the desk, and the shroud with its vent field and drive window is clearly better than the reference, although the shroud top reads a lighter grey than the rest of the onyx case.

Counts and placement match the build (three radiator fans, three front fans, one rear fan, two lit sticks, one card with a single 12V-2x6 run), the glass shows its border and a reflection, the board, combed cables and shroud carry far more detail than the reference, and the rig sits on the desk with a reflection and no hard shadow on the wall.

The perforated front has round holes with three lit fans and their hub stickers behind it, the interior shows through the reflecting glass, purple spill reaches the desk and the wall has no hard shadow, which is clearly better than the stretched perforation and plain front of the reference.

In the backplate cutout at the front end of the card there are five thick, near white horizontal bars where the GPU macro shows a fine dark fin stack, and they read as aliased or blown fin edges, even though the perforated top, the front I/O and the Vault 4 TB label seen through the shroud are clear gains over the reference.

The rear face is now finished with I/O ports and antenna jacks, an exhaust fan behind a wire grille that lights its surround, vented slot covers, and the supply with its inlet, rocker switch and honeycomb grille, all far beyond the plain rear of the reference, and the rig is grounded with no hard shadow on the wall.

With the power off every diffuser is dark, and the softboxes alone still let the radiator, pump, unlit fans, card, combed cables and shroud read clearly against the lit wall and reflective desk, with nothing floating and no blackout.

The edge of the card that faces the glass has a lit Veltrin wordmark and a saturated cyan to magenta bar that lights the 12V-2x6 cable in front of it, the brushed backplate shows the X brace, the vent row and the fin cutout, the board below has sharp labels and screws, and the whole frame is clearly richer than the reference.

The pump head has a saturated lit ring, sharp Kestrane and Tarn 360 Lux print, ribbed fittings feeding braided tubes and an X bracket with four thumbscrews, and the nearby VRM cover strip, M.2_1 plate and backplate screws are detailed, which fixes the plain cylinder fittings and smooth tubes of the reference.

Both Facet sticks have saturated, notched light bars and sharp Calyra Facet and DDR5 16 GB print that matches the two stick 16 GB kit, the 24 pin bundle is combed into a lipped grommet, and the colors are deep where the reference bars clipped to near white.

The lower board reads as a real circuit board, with traces, the M.2_3 plate, short slots, gold antenna jacks, a coin cell, the K monogram chipset whose blue accent lights the board beside it, SATA ports with a lead and mounting screws, and the GPU cable drops cleanly through a lipped grommet, well beyond the reference.

The middle front fan shows through round perforation with smoked translucent blades, a hub sticker and a lit ring that tints the blades and the edges of the mesh holes, the corner screw points are visible, and the mesh no longer has the stretched holes of the reference, though the fan frame itself is very dark.

The 24 pin bundle, which is the subject of this shot, ends on its left in a column of rounded wire stubs over the board, and no connector housing is visible anywhere, so at this zoom the cable does not visibly plug into the board, which repeats the reference's weak point about wires ending inside parts, and its two combs still read as plain bars.

The supply's rear plate is seated in the rear panel with five screw heads, and it has a beveled edge, a honeycomb grille with depth, a C14 inlet, a rocker marked I and O, and sharp 100-240 V print; the desk mirror and contact shading ground the case base, and the purple interior light falls on the shroud edge and the desk, so no fail item shows (the screw heads have no drive recess, and the inlet recess is pale grey where real ones are black).

The drive sits in a thick, rounded shroud pocket with shading where it meets the pocket walls; the PELLAM Vault 4 TB label, the barcode, the data matrix and the breather hole warning are crisp; the brushed lid with its spindle boss and Phillips screws reads as metal, and the rig's purple light falls on the right half of the lid.

The glass mid tower archetype is clear: glass with a painted border, four corner standoffs and a soft reflection; perforated front and top; tray with standoffs, grommets and a processor cutout; rear fan mount, connector cutout and a seven slot wall; vented shroud with the MIREVALE plate and a drive pocket; top front I/O and feet are all present.

The back is finished: rear fan grille, connector cutout, seven vented slot covers with a retention bar, an open supply bay with a floor vent, screw holes, feet and a perforated top, and the solid right panel shows slight roughness variation rather than a flat fill.

At close range the rounded corner pillar and the top lip catch highlights, the domed glass standoff sits on the glass corner, the glass shows a painted border and a reflection, the round front perforation is clean with no moire, and the rubber grommet through the glass is beveled.

Every listed board feature is present with true counts: four latched memory slots, three M.2 plates, a reinforced graphics slot plus shorter slots, six SATA ports in three stacked pairs, the socket and its frame, finned heatsinks, 24 pin and 8 pin power, coin cell and screwed mounting holes; the blue cover strip lights the heatsink fins and the magenta chipset accent lights the board beside it without clipping.

The silhouette reads as a 360 liquid cooler with three ring lit fans with hub stickers over a fin core and end tanks, braided tubes in smooth curves into the pump fittings, and a ring lit pump with bracket arms; the pink, purple and cyan rings are saturated and color their frames and the turntable.

The radiator back is a real tube and fin core lit through by the fan rings in graded color, with end tanks, fan frame screw holes on the top rail, and braided tubes looping cleanly to two ringed fittings on one end tank, so the back is as finished as the front.

Close on the pump, the KESTRANE and TARN 360 LUX text is crisp, the two saturated rings light the glossy cap and the body rim, the braid weave and the chrome compression rings read correctly, and the knurled thumbscrew on its bracket arm shows the fastening.

The 3.5 inch drive reads at a glance: a black cast body with three side mounting holes, a brushed lid with perimeter screws, spindle boss, breather hole and print, and a PELLAM Vault 4 TB label with a text grid, barcode, data matrix and colored corner tab that matches the catalog.

The underside is finished: a green circuit board with traces, labeled chip packages, passives and corner screws, SATA power and data connectors at the far end, mounting holes in the cast body and a spun metal motor disc, with the body's seams and side holes visible.

At the closest view the label type, the spec grid, the barcode and the footer line are sharp and unstretched, the spindle boss has a beveled rim and a machined finish around a Phillips screw, and the brushed lid and the lid screw hold detail with no tiling.

The steel box is in true ATX proportion for its 160 mm length, with a real honeycomb grille over a visible fan, light catching beveled edges, corner screws, a sharp 850W side label whose spec rows line up once perspective is allowed for, and labeled modular sockets set in rows on the inner end, and no fail list item was found.

The rear face is finished with a hex vent field, a recessed inlet, a rocker switch and a small rating print, the far side carries the same sharp label, edges catch light and the box sits on the turntable, so no fail list item was found even though the inlet reads slightly soft.

The gradient is correct (magenta violet at the rear fan, cyan at the front fans), but a cyan pool of light lies on the desk at the rear left foot of the case with no LED near it, and it matches the front fans at the far end instead of the magenta rear fan above it, so front fan light is passing through the closed steel case.

Caught near the bottom of the breath at about 12 percent, the LEDs keep the static gradient colors without clipping, the case still stands out from the wall and desk with readable edges, and no stray light pool or other fail list item appears.

Every LED shows the same lime hue as spectrum requires, but a bright green pool of light lies on the desk at the rear left foot of the case with no LED near it, which is front fan light passing through the closed steel case.

The wave correctly runs from blue cyan at the rear to magenta at the front, but a magenta pool of light lies on the desk at the rear left foot of the case, and it matches the front fans instead of the blue rear fan directly above it, so front fan light is passing through the closed steel case.

All LEDs share one purple as the shift effect requires, but a purple pool of light lies on the desk at the rear left foot of the case where no LED is near, which is front fan light passing through the closed steel case.

Each zone shows one color with a bright head and a fading tail over a dim floor as defined (a cyan arc on the rear fan, violet arcs on the front fans, a blue head on the card bar), nothing is clipped, the dark frame still reads, and no fail list item was found.

Scattered soft twinkles in all three Aurora colors sit over a dim floor on every zone as the effect defines, with no pinpoint flares, no clipping and no stray light on the desk, and the rig still reads against the wall.

At idle every zone correctly shows the cold blue, but a blue pool of light lies on the desk at the rear left foot of the case where no LED is near, which is front fan light passing through the closed steel case.

The brushed backplate has screws, a retention cross, slanted vents, the cyan ring inlay that tints the plate around it, a sharp VELTRIN CREST mark, the gold edge connector and heat pipe ends in the end window, so the back is fully finished.
At close zoom the saturated twin bars light the fins below them, the screws are seated beside the bars, the 12V-2X6 print is sharp and the bevels catch highlights.

Only the square open end cap separates this Dravik from the Veltrin Apex 3X, because the fan side uses the same rotors, hub stickers and bay dividers and the top edge repeats the Veltrin layout (wordmark at the left of a lit bar over a fin window, socket at the center, model print at the right end), which breaks the rule that a Dravik must never be mistaken for a Veltrin.

The white backplate is one flat field with no highlight or roughness variation, so it reads as paper rather than painted metal, and the right end again shows black voids instead of the pale silver fin stack.

Both light seams are saturated and not clipped, they tint the silver fins next to them, the two 8 pin sockets match the catalog, and the rounded panel edges and the Phillips screw hold up at close zoom.

The short single fan slab reads clearly against the room, with a brushed metal shroud, a fan with a sharp hub sticker, one 8 pin socket as the catalog says, a screwed bracket and a crisp wordmark, though the dark openings at the far right end are close to the limit.

The back is finished, with a brushed backplate, hex screws, a sharp DRAVIK STRATA mark, gold edge fingers with their key notch and the bracket behind, and it separates from the dark background along lit edges.

The single 8 pin socket reads as a row of H shaped posts instead of eight square pin holes, the fins in the long vent slots alias into broken staircase dashes (around x 300 to 700, y 470 to 620), and the fan at lower left is crushed nearly to black.

The chamfered three-fan shroud reads clearly against the turntable, and the 12V-2x6 socket matches the catalog. The edge bar keeps its cyan to magenta color and lights the fin stack beside it, the hub stickers and screws are present, and I found nothing from the fail list.

The slanted vents in the lower middle of the brushed backplate fill with dotted, speckled aliasing that reads as noise rather than fins behind a slot, though the cutout, heat pipe ends, gold edge connector and wordmark are all good.

At the close angle the shroud edges show bevel highlights and the screws and 12-pin socket are crisp. The 12V-2X6 print is sharp and the light bar spills blue and magenta onto the fin edges below it without clipping.

It is clearly the shorter two-fan sibling of the Apex 3X, with the same chamfered end cap and a single edge bar that lights the fin strip. Its two 8-pin sockets match the catalog and the fan hubs, bracket and screws are all present.

The three slanted vents below the X bracket show a dotted, speckled stipple that reads as aliasing rather than fins. The large VELTRIN wordmark is also crowded against the top left corner of the fin cutout on the right.

The two 8-pin sockets with 2 by 4 pin cells match the catalog, and the shroud edges are beveled with a fine grain. The cyan bar stays saturated and its purple to magenta line lights the fins beneath, and nothing on the fail list shows.

The compact two-fan Veltrin card is unlit as the catalog says and separates from the dark turntable through edge highlights. The single 8-pin socket, printed wordmark, MINI mark, hub stickers and bracket screws are all present.

Up close the 8 PIN and MINI print and the partial wordmark are sharp, and the screws and the single 8-pin socket are well formed. The shroud edges carry bevel highlights and the fin stack shows real fins through the edge slot.

The three-fan flagship shows its doubled edge bar and lit wordmark with color spilling onto the fin strip, its 12V-2x6 socket matches the catalog, and the shroud, fans and bracket are cleanly finished.

The row of slanted vents along the lower backplate is filled with speckled dot aliasing that reads as noise instead of fins, though the lit ring inlay, cutout with heat pipe ends and gold connector are correct.

The doubled light bars stay saturated blue and magenta and light the fin edges below them. The 12V-2X6 print and the screws are sharp and the inset rails and shroud edges are beveled with visible thickness.

The flat right-angled slab with a block DRAVIK wordmark is unmistakably not a Veltrin card. The fin stack shows through the long top window, the seams spill magenta onto the turntable, and the 12V-2x6 socket and three hub-stickered fans match the catalog.

The brushed graphite backplate has screws, vent cutouts and a sharp DRAVIK MONOLITH mark, the gold edge connector and exposed fin stack show along the top edge, and the magenta end seam lights the turntable at lower right.

At close zoom the edges are beveled and catch light, the single 12 pin socket matches the 12V-2x6 plug, MONOLITH is crisp, and the blue to magenta seams are saturated and tint the real fins beneath them.

The two fan flat slab reads at once, with swept blades, DRAVIK hub stickers, fins visible through the ducts, two sockets on the top edge, one colored seam lighting the fin window and a ribbed end cap.
The back is finished, with a brushed backplate, screws, slot vents, a sharp DRAVIK MONOLITH S mark, the gold fingers and PCB edge along the top and the fin stack exposed at the far end.

The two 8 pin sockets sit in recessed openings and match the catalog, the top face has fine grain and beveled edges, and the single magenta seam lights the fins pink at right while the fan blades show below.

The white three fan slab reads as white rather than grey, the faceplate has screws, the hubs carry DRAVIK stickers, the pale fins show through the ducts, and two thin seams and two sockets sit on the top edge.

The white backplate is the hero surface, and it is a featureless flat white sheet with only a faint lighter band from (150,355) to (635,545), with none of the grain or brushing its graphite siblings show, so it reads as untextured plastic.

At the closest zoom, the white top face above the sockets and the front face across the lower half are perfectly smooth, with only a lighting gradient and no paint or roughness variation, while the graphite siblings show grain at the same zoom.

The short single fan industrial card reads clearly, with a screwed brushed fan plate, a DRAVIK hub sticker, a vented two screw bracket, one 8 pin socket and a fin slot on the top edge, and a ribbed end cap, all unlit as the catalog says.
The brushed backplate has hex screws and a sharp STRATA DRAVIK mark, and a keyed gold edge connector covers about half the card's length, which fits its 172 mm, with the fin stack exposed beyond it.
At close zoom the chamfered top edge catches light, the grained top face holds a recessed 8 pin socket and crisp STRATA text, and a hex fastener and real fins with thickness are visible below.

The rig separates cleanly from a lit wall and sits on the desk with a reflection, and every part is seated. The pump ring, rear fan, front fans and light bar all throw colored light onto the board, tray, shroud and desk without clipping. It is clearly better than the reference, with readable shroud vents, drive bays, a beveled frame and glass reflections where the reference has a flat shroud block.

Straight on, the board traces, RAM, 24 pin comb, GPU wordmark and bar, shroud vents and drive cage all read, and the top fan rings light the tray in soft pools. Nothing intersects and nothing is clipped. It clearly beats the reference's flat dark board and plain shroud, although the cooler tubes are darker and harder to follow than the reference's.

The perforated front shows three ring-lit fans on mounting rails with real depth behind the mesh, the panel edge has thickness, and the glass side shows the lit interior. Fan light reaches the desk and the reflection. It is clearly better than the reference, whose mesh read as a flat dotted texture over the fans.

From above, the top mesh, the front panel button and ports, the brushed backplate with its slanted vents and X bracket, the cable cutout and the labeled 3.5 inch drive in its shroud well all read with sharp text. Light falls on the shroud and the desk. It clearly beats the reference's bare shroud and plain backplate.

The rear face now carries a full connector panel, a grilled exhaust fan lit from behind, slot covers with the card's ports and vents, a retention bar, and the supply with honeycomb, inlet and switch, all with visible edges. The interior and desk are lit by the fans. It is far better than the reference's crude fan hole and blank lower panel.

With power off and the glass off, the softboxes still give readable form everywhere: the braided tubes, the radiator label KESTRANE TARN 360 LUX, the pump head, the board, the backplate vents and the shroud with its bays. Dark diffusers are correct here, and the case is grounded with feet and a desk reflection.

The chamfered shroud, brushed backplate with vents, X bracket and flow-through cutout, the lit wordmark and the split cyan to magenta bar are all here, with sharp 12V-2x6 and APEX 3X print. The sleeved cable is plugged into a real socket and held by combs, and the bar light falls on the shroud lip and the cable. It is clearly better than the reference's flat edge face and coarse fin slot.

The pump head has a saturated cyan ring that is not clipped, sharp KESTRANE TARN 360 LUX print, ringed fittings, and an X mounting bracket with four thumb screws. The tubes read clearly as woven braid, and the VRM fins, M.2 plate and board traces are visible. It is clearly better than the reference's plain rubbery tubes and simple square mount.

The faceted, notched sticks carry saturated bars that are not clipped, with sharp CALYRA FACET DDR5 16 GB print, and the latches and four slots are present. The 24 pin connector, comb and grommet routing read cleanly, and the brushed backplate shows its vents and screws. It is clearly better than the reference's white blown-out RAM bars and tube-covered board.

The GPU fin stack seen through the side window at the top left, about x 50 to 500 and y 225 to 315, breaks into blocky stair-stepped stripes and coarse rectangles instead of even fins. Below it, the coin cell, M.2 plate, labels, screws and grommeted cable cutout are otherwise better than the reference.

Behind the perforated front with real hole depth, the smoked blades, hub sticker, screwed mounting rails and lit rings read clearly, and the ring light falls on the mesh in saturated magenta with no moire. The panel edge shows its thickness. It is clearly better than the reference's flat oval-dot texture with blades barely visible.

The 24 pin run leaves its connector straight, is held by a comb, and enters the rubber grommet slot without touching its rim. The weave of the sleeving reads as braid, the graphics cable bends smoothly into its 12V-2x6 socket, and the fan and bar light falls on the tray and board. It is clearly better than the reference's flattened, stacked 24 pin loop.

The drive's top cover to the right of the label (roughly x 920 to 1010, the full height of the bay window) is covered in heavy stretched streaks that look like a smeared texture rather than cast or brushed metal, so the cover does not read as a finished surface.

The glass mid tower is clear at a glance: the glass has a painted border, four corner standoffs and a reflection streak, the front is fine perforated steel, and the tray has grommets and standoffs, the shroud a vent field and the MIREVALE plate, and the case sits on feet and is grounded on the turntable.
The frost finish reads as white powder coat with a pale grey interior and soft shading in the seams, the glass border stays dark, and every case feature from the front shot is present and seated.

Every listed board feature is present (socket and frame, finned VRM heatsinks, four latched memory slots, three M.2 plates, chipset with the K monogram, 24 pin and processor power, coin cell, headers, screwed mounting holes), and the blue cover strip and magenta chipset accent are saturated and light the fins and the board beside them.

At close range the chokes have soft edges and sharp R22 and code labels, the capacitors show no facets, the socket frame reads as metal with corner screws over a clean pin field, and the board shows traces and sharp silk print.

The long chamfered three fan Veltrin shroud is clear in silhouette, the fans have swept blades and hub stickers over a real fin stack, and the edge bar and lit wordmark are saturated and spill onto the shroud edge and fins.

The brushed backplate has its slanted vents, end cutout showing fins and heat pipes, screwed X bracket and a sharp VELTRIN APEX 3X mark, and the gold edge connector and board edge are visible along the top.

The magenta bar at the right (around x 670 to 800, y 400 to 440) washes to pale pastel pink at its left end and the blue bar at top left goes pale at its core, so the diffusers are not saturated at their brightest.
It reads at once as the shorter two fan sibling of the Apex 3X, with the same chamfered end, edge bar and wordmark, two power sockets, a screwed bracket and finished fans over a visible fin stack.
The backplate matches the 3X family (brushed plate, slanted vents, end cutout with heat pipes, screwed X bracket, sharp APEX 2X print) with the edge connector and board edge visible.
The cyan edge bar at the top left (around x 0 to 180, y 210 to 260) washes to a near white pale cyan core instead of holding a saturated color at the diffuser.

The compact unlit two fan card reads in silhouette as a Veltrin sibling, with hub stickers, a single power socket, a printed MINI mark, a screwed bracket and a fin stack visible through the edge slot, and its form stays readable against the dark turntable.

The brushed backplate with its X brace and screws, the clean VELTRIN MINI print, the keyed gold edge connector, the chamfered Veltrin end and the bracket all read clearly, and the dark shroud still shows its form through edge highlights.

The single 2x4 socket matches 1x 8-pin, the 8 PIN and MINI print is sharp, the screws and beveled recess edges catch light, and the textured shroud, vent slats and fin stack behind the fan all read as different materials.

Three large fans with curved blades and hub stickers, a lit VELTRIN wordmark and a gradient edge bar that tints the fins below it, and a long thick chamfered shroud make it read clearly as the Veltrin flagship.

A stray bright mark sits right above the E of the VELTRIN wordmark in the center of the backplate, so it reads as an accented letter that does not match the clean wordmark on the Mini, and the rest of the backplate (ring, X brace, slanted vents, heat pipe window) is fine.

The 12V-2x6 socket and its sharp label match the catalog, the screws and beveled shroud edges catch light, and the blue and magenta bar lights the fin stack below it in saturated color without clipping.

The flat hard edged Dravik slab has three fans, the block wordmark, exposed fins through the edge windows and lit seams, with the end seam casting magenta onto the turntable, so it is clearly distinct from the Veltrin cards.
The brushed backplate has screws, a vent row and a sharp DRAVIK MONOLITH print, the gold fingers and exposed fin stack top are finished, and the lit end seam lights the turntable.
The window cutouts have beveled lips, the seams stay saturated and light the fins behind them, the socket recess and MONOLITH print are crisp, and the stepped ledges catch edge highlights.
Two fans, one continuous seam, two 8-pin sockets that match the catalog and the shared Dravik slab silhouette make it read correctly as the shorter sibling of the Monolith.

The backplate is finished with screws, vent cutouts and a sharp DRAVIK MONOLITH S print, the keyed gold fingers and fin stack top are visible, and the end face correctly has no lit seam for a one zone card.
Two 2x4 sockets with beveled recesses match the 2x 8-pin plugs, and the single seam stays saturated and lights the fins in both windows, which have real depth.

The shroud reads as true white, not grey, with crisp slab edges, three white fans with hub stickers, two 8-pin sockets, two thin seams that tint the fins in the windows, and a black steel bracket as contrast.

The white backplate has panel seams, modeled screws, a vent slot field and a sharp DRAVIK block wordmark, the gold edge fingers and silver fin stack show along the slot edge, the far end face is slotted, and the seams on the hidden edge cast purple light onto the turntable, so I found nothing from the fail list.

Two recessed 2x4 sockets match the catalog's 2x 8-pin, the thin seams stay saturated magenta and blue and tint the white faces and fins beside them, the chamfered edges catch light, the Phillips screw is modeled and the white powder coat has visible grain, which is coarse but reads as textured coating.

The slot bracket at the left shows only a column of eight identical slanted vent slits and no video port openings I can recognize, so a feature the parts list requires on every card is missing, although the single seven blade fan, hub sticker, fin stack, brushed shroud and 8 pin socket are all fine.

The brushed graphite backplate has hex screws and a sharp STRATA and DRAVIK wordmark, the gold edge fingers have their key notch, the fin stack shows at the slot edge and the slotted end face is finished, and the dark card still separates clearly from the turntable.

The thick top plate has a highlight along its chamfered edges, the single 2x4 socket matches the catalog's 1x 8-pin, real fins sit behind the vent cutouts, the hex screw is modeled, and the DRAVIK and STRATA print is sharp on the brushed metal.

The static Aurora gradient runs from pink at the rear fan through violet on the card bar to cyan at the front fans, as its definition says, every diffuser stays saturated and lights the parts and walls around it, the wall wash is soft with no hard case shadow, and the case sits grounded on the desk with its reflection.
The colors are spread as in the static frame but dimmed, as a breathing trough should be, and the case, board, card and shroud still read clearly against the lit wall and desk without blackout.

Every zone shows the same saturated green, as spectrum requires, with no clipping to white, while the sleeved cables keep their own Orchid color and the green light falls on the interior, the desk and the wall.

The colors change across the rig as one gradient, with cyan on the rear fan and pump moving to magenta and violet at the front fans and card bar, so it reads as a synced wave, and every diffuser is saturated and lights its neighbors.
Every zone shows the same saturated violet, as the shift crossfade requires, it lights the interior, desk and wall evenly, and there is no haze, flare or clipping.

Each zone shows a lit head with a dim tail at a different phase, such as the bright end of the card bar, part of one memory stick and the cyan chipset accent, over a low base glow, which fits the comet definition, and the rig still reads against the wall.
Scattered single LEDs light up in pink, violet and cyan along the fan rings, memory bars and card bar over a dim base, as starlight should, with no pinpoint flares and the case form still readable.

The blue color is right for thermal at load 0 and the rig is lit, but the supply shroud across the bottom of the onyx Vitrine reads as pale grey bare metal next to the black frame instead of black powder coat, and it is no longer the full length shroud the archetype calls for because its front section steps down into an open cage with the drive showing, while the tarn360-lux tubes from the pump up to the top radiator cannot be made out at all.

Clearly better than the reference: the glass now shows diagonal reflection streaks and corner standoffs, the case has front perforation with the three fans lighting the mesh and the desk, the shroud has a vent row, a plate and drive sleds, and I found no floating parts, intersections, haze or hard wall shadow.

Better than the reference: top ring fans cast real colored pools on the tray, the 24 pin connector and grommet are modeled, the board shows traces, and the glass reads through a soft reflection, with a grounded reflection on the desk and no clipping or blackout.

Better than the reference: the perforated front shows mounting rails with screws and three lit fans that light the mesh and the desk, the glass edge carries a highlight, and the silhouette separates clearly from the dark room with no moire or flares.

Better than the reference: the top adds front I/O with a power button, the backplate has vents and an X brace, a labeled Vault drive sits in a shroud bay, and the glass shows a reflection streak, with no intersections or pinpoint flares.

Much better than the reference: the rear now has a ported I/O cover with antenna jacks, a grilled exhaust fan, vented slot covers with a retention bar, and a supply with inlet, rocker and honeycomb grille, and the interior fans light the tray and desk.

With power off and the glass removed, the softboxes still let you read every part (braided tubes, pump text, radiator label, memory, card, board and drive sleds), the case sits on its feet with a reflection, and nothing melts into black.

Clearly better than the reference: the card has edge screws, a labeled 12V-2x6 plug, an APEX 3X print, a cutout and vents in the backplate, and a fin stack behind the window, the cyan and magenta bars light the shroud and cable without clipping, and board text such as KR-SIO and KA-ALC is sharp.

Clearly better than the reference: the braided tubes read as braid with chrome fittings, the pump has an X bracket with thumb screws and a power lead to a header, the VRM fins and M.2_1 plate are real geometry, and the KESTRANE TARN 360 LUX print is crisp.

Better than the reference: the Facet sticks have notched light bars that stay saturated and tint the backplate below them, the spreader side carries a sharp CALYRA FACET DDR5 16 GB label and a top chamfer, and the sleeved 24 pin run sits in combs at its connector.

Clearly better than the reference: the lower board shows an M.2_3 plate, short slots, a CR2032 coin cell, screw heads, fan headers with leads, and a K chipset whose blue accent lights the board beside it, and the cable drops through a rimmed shroud slot with ribbed combs.

Better than the reference: the round perforated steel reads as metal over fan rails with screws, the smoked blades and hub sticker show through it, and the lit rings spill magenta onto the mesh and rails with no moire, clipping or flares.

Better than the reference: the 24 pin has a modeled housing with a latch, the alternating purple and black braid is sharp, and a comb holds the run at a rubber grommet, though from this angle the turn into the grommet is foreshortened, so the run looks like it stops at the hole, and the 12V-2x6 run bends smoothly from its plug.

The supply's rear plate is fixed with screws and has a sharp printed voltage line, a C14 inlet with pins, a rocker in a bezel and a real honeycomb grille, and the case sits seated on the desk with contact shading and a reflection while the interior purple light reaches the shroud edge.

The Vault drive sits in the shroud recess under a thick rounded rim, with a sharp catalog label, barcode, data matrix, breather hole print, a cover screw and a raised spindle boss, and the interior purple light falls across the top cover.

The glass mid tower reads at once, with a bordered glass side carrying four corner standoffs and softbox reflections, a perforated front with fan rails and screw holes, a tray with standoffs, grommeted cutouts and a processor cutout, a rear fan mount, a slot wall, a vented shroud with the MIREVALE plate, and the front panel ports on top.

The rear is fully finished, with a rear fan grille, a tall connector cutout, seven vented slot covers under a retention bar, an open supply bay and feet, and the solid right panel shows soft tonal variation and a radiused corner against the turntable.

At close range the frame corner pillar and top rail have soft radii, the domed glass standoff is seated, the fine round perforation on the front holds without moire, the tray grommet has a raised lip, and a reflection streak shows the glass.

The single tower has a dense black fin stack with separate fins, twelve nickel pipe caps for six pipes through a beveled top plate with the wordmark, an unlit fan held by steel wire clips with a hub sticker, nickel pipes at the base and a cross bracket with spring screws.

The back is as finished as the front: the exit face of the fin stack shows every fin edge, and the clipped fan frame, the base pipes, the contact block and the bracket screws are all present and seated.

The brushed top plate has a beveled edge, sharp KESTRANE and PILLAR 120 print and domed nickel pipe caps seated in shadowed holes, and the rounded fin edges and the wire clip on the fan corner hold up at this zoom.
The lit ring is saturated blue and not clipped, it lights the blades, the frame face and the turntable in front of it, and the rest of the tower keeps the Pillar's fin stack, caps, clips and bracket.
From behind, the fin exit face is fully finished, and the ring's blue spill shows on the fan edge, on the nearby fins and on the turntable on that side, which fits where the fan points.

Close up, the wire clip hooks into a real hole in a radiused frame corner, the open duct shows between the flanges, the ring is blue and not white and lights the frame face and blades, and the hub sticker text is sharp.

The dual tower has two separate fin stacks with their own top plates, wordmarks and pipe caps, a clipped fan between the towers and one on the front, nickel pipes at the base and a sprung cross bracket, so it reads clearly as the wider sibling of the Pillar.

Both fan rotors, the front fan on the left tower and the fan between the towers, sink into flat black inside their frames, so no blade shape can be read and only the frame edges and one faint curve show.

The top plate has a beveled edge and fine surface grain, the KESTRANE and TWIN PILLAR print is sharp, the nickel heat pipe caps sit in countersunk holes, and the wire clip, fan frame radius and fin thickness all hold at close range.

The pump ring is saturated blue and lights the turntable and the nearby fan blades, the two unlit fans match the catalog count and have hub stickers and corner screws, and the braided tubes, silver fittings and bracket thumbscrews all read as their materials.

The radiator back shows a real tube and fin core with end tanks, fittings on the tank and braided tubes looping cleanly over the top, and the pump light seen through the fin gaps fits its source behind the core.

The fans on this cooler are unlit, but the lower left blades of the far left fan and the lower left corner of the radiator frame glow bright blue, more than the middle fan right behind the pump, so the light looks like it comes from an unlit fan and not from the pump ring.

Three fan positions show along the top edge, the fin core and end tanks have form and edge highlights, the braided tubes leave the tank fittings and curve over cleanly, and the light through the core matches where the pump sits.

Three lit ring fans and the pump ring stay saturated in pink, violet and cyan without clipping, each lights its own blades, frame and the turntable, and the hubs, screws, tubes and fittings are all finished.
The pink and blue ring fan light comes through the fin core where each fan sits and spills onto the turntable, and the tanks, fittings and braided tube loop are finished and seated.

The long chamfered shroud has three fans with shaped blades and VELTRIN hub stickers, the edge bar and lit wordmark stay colored and light the fin slot below them, and the single 12V-2x6 socket matches the catalog.

The brushed backplate carries slanted vents, a cutout showing fins and heat pipes, a screwed X bracket and sharp VELTRIN APEX 3X print, the gold edge connector and board edge show at the top, and the bar lights the turntable below.

At close range the 12V-2x6 socket has pins and sharp print, the screws are seated, the shroud has grain and beveled edges, and the blue and magenta bar segments stay colored while lighting the fin stack under them.

It reads at once as the shorter two fan sibling of the Apex 3X, with the same chamfered shroud, two fans with hub stickers, two 8 pin sockets that match the catalog, and one edge bar that is saturated and lights the fins beneath it.

The brushed backplate has its X brace, screws, three slanted vents and a cutout showing the fin stack and heat pipe ends, the gold edge connector has its key notch, the wordmark is sharp, and the edge bar lights the turntable purple under the card.

The two 8 pin sockets match the catalog, the cyan to magenta edge bar stays saturated and lights the exposed fins below it, the shroud has fine texture and beveled steps, and the screw and fan ring hold up at this zoom.

Two fans with curved blades and hub stickers, one 8 pin socket, a bracket with screws and a chamfered end cap all match the unlit compact card, and the dark body still separates from the turntable and background.
The plain brushed backplate has an X brace, screws and a sharp VELTRIN MINI mark, the gold connector and its notch are present, and the chamfered shroud end is finished.
The 8 PIN and MINI print is crisp, the single 8 pin socket, screws, exposed fin slot, beveled shroud steps and textured surface all hold at close zoom.

Three fans, the lit wordmark and one 12V-2x6 socket are correct, but the light bars at the two ends of the top edge (top left by the wordmark and the upper bar at the right end) read pale lavender and pale pink instead of saturated color.

The backplate has a saturated cyan ring inlay with a soft halo, a row of slanted vents, an X brace, a sharp VELTRIN CREST mark and a cutout showing four heat pipes, and the edge bar lights the turntable blue under the card.

The long light rod at the top left and its twin at the right edge are washed out to near white with only a faint lavender tint, and the magenta block at the right has a pastel pink top, so these diffusers do not hold saturated color even though the bars below them light the fins well.

The flat slab with its hard edges, three fans with DRAVIK hubs, exposed fin windows, a 12V-2x6 socket and three light seams (two on the top edge and one vertical seam on the end) match the catalog, and the end seam lights the turntable magenta.
The brushed slab backplate has screws, a vent row, a sharp DRAVIK MONOLITH block mark, the gold connector and an exposed fin edge, and the vertical end seam lights the turntable.
The thin blue and magenta seams are saturated and light the fins in both windows, the 12V-2x6 socket and MONOLITH print are sharp, and the stepped edges carry bevel highlights.

Two fans, two 8 pin sockets, a single gradient seam along the top edge that lights the fin windows, and a ribbed end on the flat slab all match the catalog, and the shape clearly reads as the Monolith's smaller sibling.

The black slot bracket at the left melts into the black background so that only its top tab and a thin edge line can be read, the right end face with its vents is close to black, and the row of rectangular cutouts with two small sockets low in the middle of the backplate looks like stray openings rather than a recognizable feature.

The single seam is a saturated blue to magenta that is not clipped and it tints the fins in both nearby windows, the two 8 pin sockets and the window recesses have beveled edges, the plate shows brushing, and there is no faceting on the fan opening.

The white slab reads as white with crisp but highlighted edges, it has three swept fans with hub stickers, two colored seams that light the pale fin stack behind the top windows, power sockets, and a perforated bracket with its screw, and nothing is clipped or floating within the part.

This is a short single fan unlit Dravik slab with a raised brushed fan plate held by four screws, a single 8 pin socket, a wordmark on the top edge, a hub sticker, and a two tone bracket with screws, and the silhouette separates clearly from the dark backdrop.

The backplate is finished, with brushing, hex screws and a sharp DRAVIK STRATA mark, the gold edge connector stands proud of the board edge, and the bracket, the fin opening and the vented end face all stay readable against the dark turntable.

At close range the window and socket recesses have beveled edges, the STRATA print is sharp, the 2x4 socket cavities and the hex head fastener are modeled, and the brushed plate has visible variation, with no shimmer or faceting.

This reads as a 3.5 inch drive in true proportion, with a cover held by perimeter screws, a spindle cap, a breather hole with its print, a sharp label with a barcode and a data matrix, side mounting holes, and a rounded cast base with a seam line.

The metal cover in the lower left quarter, below and left of the spindle cap, carries cloudy dark blotches that read as grime or fingerprints rather than clean stainless metal, even though the label text and barcode above are sharp.

The box is steel with rounded corners and corner screws, a honeycomb grille over a visible fan, a sharp 850W side label with a spec table, and a recessed modular panel with labeled sockets, and it reads as at least three distinct materials.

On the rear face the power inlet is a plain grey block in a square bezel with no keyed socket outline and no three pins, and the face shows none of the four mounting screw holes a supply uses to fix to the case, so the rear does not hold up when you lean in.

The static gradient flows front to rear as defined, from cyan front fans through the violet memory and a magenta to blue card bar to the magenta rear fan, the diffusers stay saturated, the light spills onto the board, the shroud and the desk reflection, and there are no flares or hard wall shadow.

This is the same hue layout as static at a lower breathing level, which matches the definition, and the case edges, the parts and the desk reflection still read against the lit wall with no blackout, clipping or flare.

Every LED zone shows the same saturated green, as the spectrum effect requires: the four ring fans, the pump ring, both memory bars, the card bar, the wordmark and the board strips. The green spills onto the board, the shroud top, the desk and the wall. The rings stay green and do not clip to white. The case separates from the background, the reflection grounds it on the desk, and the VELTRIN, KESTRANE, KORRIN and MIREVALE marks are sharp.

The Aurora stops spread across the rig as one wave: cyan at the rear fan and pump, violet at the memory, cyan into magenta along the card bar, and magenta and violet at the front fans. Each diffuser stays saturated and lights the interior, the desk and the wall in matching colors. There is no haze, no flare and no hard wall shadow.

Every zone shows the same Aurora violet, as the shift crossfade requires. The color is saturated at the rings and bars and washes the interior, the shroud, the desk reflection and the wall evenly. The case edges, glass border, reflection streaks and text all hold.

Most LEDs sit near the dim floor, while bright heads with fading tails show on the rear fan ring, the lower memory bar and the left end of the card bar. The wordmark takes a different stop because its zone has its own phase. The frame is dark by design, but the case outline, shroud, board and desk reflection still read, so it does not fail X15.

Individual LEDs twinkle in different Aurora stops (cyan, magenta, violet) across the card bar, memory bars and fan rings, as starlight requires. The points are soft lit blobs, not pinpoint flares, and the cool fill keeps the case, shroud and desk readable against the wall.

At load 0 every zone sits at the cold blue end of the thermal scale, which fits idle temperatures. The blue stays saturated at the rings and bars, lights the board, the shroud top, the desk reflection and the wall, and the frame keeps clear silhouettes and sharp marks.
