Clearly better than the reference: the glass shows its corner standoffs and reflection streaks, the board shows traces, the cable combs and grommeted 24 pin are visible, the shroud has drive sleds, and the pump ring, memory bars and front rings light their surroundings and the desk reflection; the only point where it does not beat the reference is that the cooler tubes are much less visible because they run tight under the radiator.

Better than the reference: the top has fine perforation with no moire, the front I/O cluster and power button sit on the top right, the panel edges show thickness, the backplate shows its bracket and vents, the drive label reads through the shroud window, and the rig is grounded with a colored desk reflection.

Much richer than the reference's plain rear: it has a real connector block with antenna posts and ports, a round wire grille with the lit exhaust fan behind it, screwed slot covers on a retention bar, and a supply rear with honeycomb, inlet and rocker switch, while the lit front rings show through the glass and the feet sit in a reflection.

Power off, glass off, softbox lit, and every part still reads: the radiator side print, the black tubes looping to the rear end tank, the unlit smoked fans, the board traces, the sleeved cables and the shroud sleds, with the case seated on its feet in a desk reflection and nothing blacked out.

Clearly better than the reference: the brushed backplate has its X bracket, vent row and cutout, the edge has the 12V-2x6 socket with a seated plug and sharp VELTRIN and APEX 3X print, the bar colors are saturated and spill onto the sleeves, and the pump, M.2 heatsink, board silkscreen and shroud vent field all hold detail.

The supply's rear plate is screwed at four corners and has a recessed IEC inlet, a rocker switch marked I and O, sharp 100-240 V print and a honeycomb grille with depth; the steel shows subtle variation, the slot covers and retention bar sit above, and the case base meets its desk reflection, with the hex cells cut off at the grille's right edge as the only minor weakness.

The Vault 4 TB label is crisp and has a barcode, data matrix and spec grid, and it sits on a dark cast cover with a screwed spindle boss inside a shroud window with real wall thickness and rounded corners; nearby LED light falls on the right of the cover, and sleeved cables show through the neighboring pass-through.

A single tower with a dense black fin stack, twelve nickel pipe ends through a stamped top plate carrying the wordmark, nickel pipes into a plated base, a cross mounting bracket with screws, an unlit fan held by steel wire clips at top and bottom, and a hub sticker, all seated on the turntable with contact shading.

The back is as finished as the front: the exhaust face shows separate fin plates with real gaps and stepped edges, the wordmark reads correctly rotated on the top plate, the fan edge and both wire clips show at the side, and the heat pipes, base and bracket are fully modeled underneath.

At close zoom the top plate has a rounded beveled edge, a fine brushed texture and sharp KESTRANE and PILLAR 120 print, the domed nickel pipe caps sit in their holes, the fin plates have visible thickness, and the wire clip catches a highlight.

It differs from Pillar exactly by its lit ring fan, and the ring stays a saturated blue rather than white while lighting the blades, the frame interior and the turntable; the rest of the tower keeps all its Pillar features and detail.

The rear fin face, top plate wordmark, clips, pipes and bracket are fully finished, and the hidden ring fan's blue light spills realistically from the fan edge onto the turntable and the background on that side.

The ring diffuser is a saturated cyan, not white, and lights the frame's inner faces blue, the wire clip hooks into a beveled corner pad, the heat pipe caps sit in recessed holes, and the top plate wordmark and the hub sticker are sharp.

Both fin stacks, with seven pipe caps on each top plate, read clearly, the front fan and the fan between the towers are wire clipped, and the X bracket with four screws and the exposed pipes finish the base, though the middle fan's interior sits close to black.

The rear fin face is finished with distinct beveled fins, the middle fan is clipped to the rear tower, which matches the front view, and the base bracket, the screws and the contact plate are all modeled.

The top plate has a beveled edge and a brushed variation, the KESTRANE and TWIN PILLAR print is crisp, the polished pipe caps sit in countersinks, and the wire clip seats against the frame with a believable highlight.
It reads at once as a low profile top down cooler, with a slim fan screwed at its corners onto a flat fin stack, the wordmark on the side plate, and a seated mounting bracket with screws.

Four nickel heat pipes curve smoothly up out of the base into the fin stack, which matches the catalog, the back side is finished with its plate and fins, and the bracket and contact plate are grounded.

Up close the fins have thickness and rounded tips, the knurled slotted mounting screws and the brushed bracket edges are beveled, the fan corner screw and fan cable are present, and the contact plate reads as metal.

The pump ring is a saturated cyan to violet and pools colored light on the plinth and the nearby fan blades, the braided tubes curve smoothly, the two unlit fans carry sharp hub stickers, and the radiator end tanks and fill port are present.
The radiator back shows a real fin core between the end tanks, the braided tubes loop over and into two fittings on the end tank, and pump light shows faintly through the core.

The pump ring is saturated and unclipped and tints the cap face, the KESTRANE and TARN 240 text is crisp, the braid weave and ribbed chrome fittings hold up close, and the bracket thumbscrew is modeled.

White reads as white, the two lit fan rings (magenta and cyan) and the pump ring tint their own frames, blades and the plinth, and the white braided tubes and radiator end tank are clean, though the pump ring's left edge runs close to pale.

Two lit fans and a lit pump sit directly against this white radiator, yet the fin core on the back shows none of their magenta or cyan light, while the graphite sibling's back shows its pump light through the core, so the lit zones fail to light the surface they are bolted to.

The cyan to violet pump ring glows but the white face inside it and the white housing next to it stay plain grey white with almost no colored spill, while the black Tarn 360 face shows clear blue spill from the same ring, so the light does not reach the surfaces nearest to it.

The 360 radiator with three unlit fans, braided tubes, chrome fittings, a bracketed pump with a lit blue ring and readable hub stickers all read clearly, and the pump casts a blue pool on the turntable that seats the part.

The back has a finished fin core between end tanks, fan mount openings along the top edge and tubes that seat cleanly in chrome fittings on the end tank, with no moire and good contact shading on the turntable.

The close view has sharp KESTRANE and TARN 360 text, a beveled rim, brushed housing, a slotted thumbscrew, banded chrome fittings and braid weave, and the colored ring visibly tints the dark glass face blue.
Three saturated ring fans in magenta, blue and cyan tint their smoked blades, the radiator frame and the turntable, and the pump ring and bracket screws read cleanly with no clipping or haze.
The fan light coming through the fin core from behind is believable, the end tanks and fittings are finished, the tubes arc smoothly, and the colored pool on the turntable grounds the radiator.
The text is sharp, the edges are beveled, the fittings and thumbscrew are detailed, and the blue ring lights the dark face, with the lit fans behind adding colored context without blowing out.

The long, thick, chamfered Veltrin shroud with three large fans, brushed faces, an edge bar that lights the fin stack beneath it, a bracket with vents and a 12V-2x6 socket reads clearly as the flagship and is grounded by its shadow.

At close range the 12V-2x6 label is sharp, socket pins and screws are present, the shroud has fine texture and beveled edges, and the blue and pink bars visibly light the real fins of the exposed stack.

The flat Dravik slab has three fans, an exposed fin stack through the edge window, a block wordmark and three separate light seams (top, window and end) that light the fins and pool magenta on the turntable.

The brushed backplate has screws, a vent field, a sharp DRAVIK MONOLITH mark, the board edge with gold contacts and the lit end seam spilling onto the turntable, so the back is as finished as the front.

The shorter two fan slab clearly belongs to the Monolith family, with a single lit seam along the top window lighting the fins, an unlit end, a vented bracket and two power sockets, which matches its one zone.

The two power sockets sit in the middle of the backplate face, lower right beside the four vent slots, instead of on the edge that faces the glass where the world rules put card power plugs (the Halide has plain vent slots in the same spot), so the card disagrees with the build's placement rule.

The white slab silhouette, three white fans with shaped blades and hub stickers, the two colored light seams that tint the fins in their windows, the power sockets on the top edge, the black bracket and the soft shadow on the turntable all read correctly, and I found no item from the fail list.

The backplate is finished with recessed panels, screws, a vent field and a sharp DRAVIK and HALIDE mark, the gold edge connector and the pale fin stack window show along the top edge, the bracket edge catches a highlight, and the white reads as white without blackout or uniform-surface faults.

The cast black body with side mounting holes, the screwed metal top cover with its pressed center ring and breather hole print, and the sharp Pellam label with barcode give three clear materials with beveled lit edges, and nothing floats or intersects.

At the close view the label text, spec table and barcode stay crisp, the cover edge carries a bevel highlight, the screws have modeled cross recesses, and the pressed ring and cover grain give the metal visible variation.

The steel box has beveled lit edges and corner screws, a real honeycomb grille over a visible fan on top, a sharp 850W side label with a spec table, and a rear face with an inlet, a rocker switch and a honeycomb vent, and it separates cleanly from the dark backdrop.

The colors hold still as a front to rear gradient, cyan on the front fans running to magenta on the rear fan and the card bar, and they wash the case interior, the wall and the desk mirror with no clipping, flare or blackout.

Every zone shows the static gradient's colors scaled down together as the breathing definition says, and the case, parts and desk still read clearly with edges and reflection, so there is no blackout.

Every zone, from the fans, pump ring and memory bars to the card bar, shows the same saturated green as spectrum requires, and that green spills onto the interior, the wall and the desk reflection without clipping to white.

The colors change across the rig as one synced gradient, cyan at the rear fan and pump moving through blue on the memory to magenta on the front fans, and the card bar runs cyan to magenta along its length, which matches the wave definition, with the light reaching nearby surfaces.
Every LED shows the same violet as shift requires, the color is saturated and not clipped, and it lights the interior, the wall and the desk mirror evenly.

Each zone shows its own bright head with a fading trail, seen as part rings on the fans and pump and as partly lit memory bars, and the zones are offset in phase and color as the comet definition says, while the darker frame still keeps the case edges and desk readable.

With starlight's dim base level the board sinks into a dark navy blur below and to the right of the pump, between the RAM and the cable grommet and behind the graphics power cable, so the heatsinks, chokes and slot detail cannot be read, and the case front and top faces nearly disappear into the dark wall.

The thermal mapping is right, with every zone in the same cold blue at load 0 and blue light falling on the shroud, board and desk, but the lit VELTRIN wordmark on the card edge washes out to a pale near-white blue under the deep blue edge bar instead of staying saturated.

Clearly better than the reference: the glass shows its painted border, corner fixings and soft reflection streaks, the front fans light the mesh and the desk, the wall picks up the rig's purple, the case sits on a mirrored desk with contact shading, and I found no haze, flare, floating part or intersection.

Better than the reference: the radiator rings, pump ring, card edge bar and front fans each light the board, tray and back wall, the 24 pin and graphics runs enter real grommet cutouts with combs, and the frame is free of blackout, flare and hard wall shadow.

Better than the reference: the round perforated front reads as steel with the three lit fans and their rails behind it, the glass edge and border are visible, the fans light the desk and its reflection, and the rig separates cleanly from the dark room.

Better than the reference: the perforated top, front I/O with power button, brushed backplate with X bracket and vents, and the Vault label seen through the shroud window all hold up, and the glass and desk reflections ground the case with no flare or haze.

Better than the reference: the rear now shows a real I/O block, a wire fan grille, slot covers with a retention bar, and a supply face with inlet, rocker switch and honeycomb, while the interior light falls on the desk and the rear panel stays readable instead of melting into black.

The card itself beats the reference (chamfered shroud, brushed backplate with X bracket and cutout, lit wordmark, 12V-2x6 socket, combed braid) but the two memory light bars at top center read as flat painted blue and violet plastic and throw no color onto the pump flank or slots right beside them.

Braided tubes, chrome fittings, thumbscrew bracket and sharp TARN 360 LUX print are clearly better than the reference, but the two memory light bars on the right are saturated solid color with no spill onto the dark slot and spreader between them or the board around them, so they glow without lighting anything.

This is the memory's own macro and its two light bars read as flat blue and violet painted plastic with no halo, no frosted depth and no light falling on the black pump flank, the neighboring spreader or the backplate at their feet, so it does not beat the reference's lit bars on light even though the label and notch detail are better.

Clearly better than the reference: traces, coin cell, short slots, SATA ports with thin black leads, Phillips mounting screws, the lit K chipset plate spilling blue onto the board, the edge bar lighting the fin stack and the combed cable entering a rubber edged shroud cutout all hold, though the tiny REV and coin cell print is right at the edge of legible.

Better than the reference: the round perforation reads as steel with depth and no moire, the smoked blades and hub sticker show behind it, the lit ring tints the mesh around it, and the fan rails with their screws seat the fans against the front.

The 24 pin run is better than the reference (individually braided wires, comb, straight exit from the plug into a rubber grommet slot) but the memory light bars in the center of the frame show no light at all on the pure black pump flank right beside them.

The supply is reduced to a rear plate with a generic voltage line and no Thessic mark or catalog capacity anywhere in frame, and its honeycomb opens onto a flat black void with no fan, heatsink or interior form behind it, so the subject cannot be read as a finished part.

The Vault drive sits in a beveled shroud window with a thick rim, its label print and barcode stay sharp at this zoom, the screw and breather mark are present, and the purple LED spill lights the cover around the spindle dome.
On both lit fans the radiator fin lines show crisply through the white blades across the whole duct, so the blades read as clear film rather than solid or frosted plastic.

The white radiator reads white, with a real flat tube and fin core lit softly by the fans behind it, end tanks, frame screws and braided tubes leaving their fittings cleanly, so the back is as finished as the front.

The pump face, the fittings, the braid and the KESTRANE TARN 240 FROST print hold up, but across the top band the fan blades again show the radiator's horizontal fin lines sharply through them, so the blades read as transparent.

The silhouette clearly shows a chamfered three fan Veltrin card, and the edge light bar is saturated and tints the fin grille below it, with a lit wordmark, a power socket, hub stickers and a bracket with its screw.

Apart from a brushed shroud texture this is the Apex 3X front again: the same silhouette, fan size, light bar gradient, socket position and end chamfer, with nothing that shows it is the thickest and longest flagship with larger fans that its row describes.

A flat brushed Dravik slab with a sharp block wordmark, backplate screws, gold edge fingers, a deep fin stack in the long window and a magenta seam on the end face that tints the face and the turntable.

The two fan right angled slab reads clearly in silhouette, and its single edge seam is saturated and lights the fin windows, with hub stickers, a bracket screw, two power sockets and a vented end face present.

The brushed backplate is finished with screws, the DRAVIK MONOLITH S print is sharp, and the gold fingers, the exposed fin stack, the vented end face and the bracket are all present and read as their materials.

At close range the brushed top face, the chamfered socket recesses with real pin cells and the beveled edge strips hold up, and the saturated seam tints the neighboring chamfer and the fins in both windows.
The slab reads as true white rather than grey, with screws, panel lines, a sharp DRAVIK HALIDE print, pale silver fins through the side window, gold fingers and a dark bracket.

The lit rig separates from the wall, and the static Aurora colors are saturated and unclipped on the fans, pump, memory and card bar, with their light reaching the interior, the desk reflection and the wall, and no haze or flare.

Caught at a low point in the pulse, the LEDs keep the static Aurora spread (teal-blue front fans, purple rear fan, pump and RAM) and still light the board's right side, while the case, GPU and shroud stay readable against the purple wall with no blackout, clipping or flare.

Every LED (fans, pump ring, RAM bars, GPU bar, wordmark and chipset accent) shows the same saturated green as the definition requires, and that green carries onto the interior, the desk and the wall without clipping or haze.

The gradient flows across the whole rig as one, from blue and teal at the rear fan and pump to magenta at the front fans, with the GPU bar shading cyan to pink along its length, and each zone colors the surfaces and desk next to it without clipping.
Every zone shows the same saturated purple stop, which washes the interior, the shroud top, the desk and the wall, and the ring diffusers stay colored rather than white.

Each zone shows its own head and fading tail at a different phase (cyan arc on the rear fan, pink-lit wordmark, purple low on the RAM, teal chipset accent), the rest stays at a dim floor, and the frame keeps its form without blackout.
Single LEDs twinkle as soft colored spots on the GPU bar, fan rings and RAM over a dim base, as the definition describes, with no hard pinpoint flares and with the rig still separating from the wall.

At load 0 every zone sits at the same cold blue the thermal mapping gives, the blue lights the board, the shroud, the desk and the wall, and the fan rings stay saturated blue rather than clipping to white.

The supply's rear plate has four screws, a recessed inlet, a rocker marked I and O, a deep honeycomb grille and sharp THESSIC 850W print, sits flush in a beveled matte steel rear panel with subtle variation, and is grounded with a desk reflection.

The Vault 4 TB label is sharp down to its small spec grid, barcode and breather-hole note, the bay rim has rounded thickness, purple light falls into the bay and onto the cover, and the drive reads as seated under the shroud lip with its hub screw and label screw in place.

The chunky three fan card has a brushed shroud, a chamfered end cap, curved bladed fans with hub stickers, and an edge bar and lit VELTRIN wordmark whose spectrum light spills onto the fin stack, and the silhouette separates from the dark disc.

The steel box has corner screws, an orange peel top, a real honeycomb grille over a visible fan, a side label with a large 850W and a readable spec table, and a recessed modular panel with pinned sockets labeled down to 12V-2x6.
The rear face is finished with hex perforation, a modeled inlet with pins, a rocker switch, corner screws and a small printed rating line, and the matching side label and grille hold up.

The seven fans, pump ring, GPU bars and lit chipset accent all throw colored light onto the tray and shroud, the cables arrive in the grommet and the GPU socket with combs, the feet are seated with a reflection, and the whole frame reads clearly better than the murky reference.

The silhouette clearly reads as a long chamfered three fan Veltrin card. The fan count matches the catalog. The edge light bar and lit wordmark tint the exposed fin stack below them, and the bracket, screws and hub stickers are all present with a shadow seating the card on the turntable.

At closest zoom, the top edge surface between the light bar and the fin window (center band, roughly x 300 to 800) carries a coarse blotchy bump noise that reads as stucco or leatherette, not as molded plastic or anodized metal, although the socket, screws, 12V-2x6 print and lit fins hold up.

It reads as a shorter two fan sibling of the Apex 3X with the same chamfered end cap. It has two 8-pin sockets as the catalog says and a single edge bar that tints the fin stack, and the printed wordmark, bracket screws and contact shadow are all in place.

The shroud top around the two sockets has a heavy mottled noise that reads as stucco rather than plastic or metal, and the light bar at the top left is washed to a pale near white cyan at its core instead of a saturated diffuser color.

It is a compact two fan Veltrin card, unlit as the catalog says. It has one 8-pin socket, a printed wordmark and MINI mark, a chamfered end cap, bracket thumbscrews and hub stickers, and it stays readable against the dark turntable with a contact shadow.

Across the whole top edge (upper half of the frame, around the TRIN wordmark, socket and MINI text), the surface shows large blotchy grain that reads as pebbled leather or stucco instead of a believable plastic or metal finish, even though the text and screws are sharp.

It reads as the thick three fan Veltrin flagship. The brushed fan face reads as metal and the bright chamfer trims and edge bar light the fin stack, and the fan count, lit wordmark, bracket and grounding shadow are all correct.

The top edge plate around the 12V-2x6 socket and between the blue and pink bars (center right, roughly x 300 to 800, y 280 to 430) carries the same coarse blotchy noise, so at closest zoom it reads as stucco rather than plastic or metal, although the bars do light the fins and the trim edge catches light.

It reads as a flat Dravik slab with hard angles, a block wordmark and two exposed fin windows. There are three thin seams, matching three zones: the top run, the right window and the end face. The seams tint the fins they border, the three fans have hub stickers, and the slab is shaded onto the turntable.

At closest zoom, the brushed top plate reads as metal and the window and socket openings have beveled edges. The MONOLITH print and 12V-2x6 pins are crisp, and the blue and pink seams visibly light the fins inside both windows.

It reads as the shorter two fan Dravik slab with a single seam, as its one zone requires. It has two 8-pin sockets as the catalog says, exposed fin windows tinted by the seam, a ribbed end face, a bracket with screws and a contact shadow.
The brushed plate reads as metal, the two 8-pin socket recesses are beveled with sharp pin marks, the single magenta seam runs cleanly along the bevel, and the fin windows show real fins lit by it.

Three white fans with hub stickers and a clean white Dravik slab with screws at the fan frame corners, a silver fin stack in two side windows, two light seams that tint the fins and the shroud next to them, and two sockets that match the 2x 8-pin, with no fail item found.

The pale brushed backplate has recessed panels, screws, a sharp DRAVIK wordmark with a HALIDE line, gold edge fingers, the fin stack along the edge and a ribbed end face, so the back is as finished as the front and nothing intersects or blacks out.

At this close zoom every white surface, the top rim and the face around the two power sockets and the screw, has a coarse, blotchy, bumpy grain that reads as stucco or foam board, not the flat white slab faces with crisp edges that the Halide row calls for.

A short, unlit, single fan Dravik card in a brushed fan plate with four screws, with louvered end vents, one 8 pin socket, a two screw bracket and a backplate edge visible, and the dark shroud is shaded enough against the dark turntable that its form still reads.

The brushed top plate has a chamfered edge that catches light, sharp DRAVIK and STRATA print, real fins seen through the vent slots, a recessed 8 pin socket and a hex head fastener on the side, with no fail item found.

Clearly better than the reference: the glass shows a painted border, corner standoffs and diagonal reflections, the shroud now has a vent field, drive cage cutouts and a brand plate, the braided tubes, pump, RAM, card and 24 pin comb are all seated, the purple front fans light the desk and reflection, and I found no haze, flare, float or intersection.

Clearly better than the reference: the three lit top fans, the rear fan, the edge-on front fan rings and the cyan to magenta card bar each light the tray and board near them, the glass carries soft streaks, the case sits on a clean reflection with contact glow under the feet, and every part reads in silhouette with nothing crossing anything.

Clearly better than the reference: the fine round perforated front shows real holes over three lit fans on screwed mounting rails, the purple light falls on the rails, the floor and the reflection, the soft wall falloff has no hard case shadow, and even with the dark left background the case edge and glass frame still separate clearly.

Clearly better than the reference: the perforated top, the front I/O with power button and ports, the brushed backplate with slanted vents and an X brace, the drive label through the shroud cutout and the glass streak all hold up, and the rig is grounded with a clean desk reflection and no clipping or blackout.

Clearly better than the reference, which had a plain rear: the rear face is now finished with the connector block, antenna posts, a round fan grille, slot covers on a retention bar, and a supply face with a honeycomb, inlet, rocker switch and label, while the lit interior and the desk reflection read cleanly.

With the power off and only the softboxes lighting it, every part still reads: the radiator label, pump head, braided tubes, card, combs and drive cage are distinct in dark steel, aluminum, PCB and braid, the case has its corner fixings and feet seated on the reflective desk, and nothing melts into black.

Clearly better than the reference: the chamfered shroud has edge screws, a separate cyan bar and magenta bar beside a crisp VELTRIN and APEX 3X, a labelled 12V-2x6 socket with a modeled plug, a brushed backplate with an X brace, slanted vents and a fin cutout, and fins and fans visible through the lower window, with all text sharp.

Clearly better than the reference: the lathed pump has a saturated cyan ring, a sharp KESTRANE and TARN 360 LUX, ringed metal fittings, an X bracket held by four thumbscrews and a thin power lead, and the woven braided tubes bend smoothly up toward the radiator without crossing anything.

Clearly better than the reference, whose light bars blew out to white: the two Facet sticks now have saturated blue and purple notched bars, a faceted dark spreader with a sharp CALYRA FACET DDR5 16 GB label and slot latches, and they sit beside a 24 pin connector with individually sleeved wires through a comb and a pump lead plugged into a header.

Clearly better than the reference: the board shows traces, small print (KR-SIO, KA-ALC, CR2032), a coin cell, an M.2 heatsink, gold audio caps, screwed mounting holes, fan headers with leads and a K monogram chipset whose blue accent lights the board beside it, and the sleeved card cable runs through three combs into a beveled shroud grommet.

Clearly better than the reference: the front shows clean round perforations with no moire over smoked swept blades and a hub sticker, the fans sit on screwed mounting rails that the magenta rings visibly light, and the frame, rails and glass side keep their form against the dark.

Clearly better than the reference: the 24 pin run shows twelve alternating purple and black braided wires leaving a latched connector straight through a comb into a rounded grommet, the card cable curls cleanly from its labelled 12V-2x6 plug, and the board edge, RAM label and pump lead are all sharp, with no wire crossing a part.
The top left screw head on the supply's rear plate sits on the T of the printed THESSIC 850W label, so a fastener and the print collide in the most legible corner of the macro.

The top panel reads as a smooth solid sheet with no perforation anywhere, while the front mesh shows its holes clearly, so the perforated top over the radiator mount that the Vitrine row calls for is missing.
The frost top panel is a plain unbroken white sheet with no perforation over the radiator mount, and the MIREVALE plate on the shroud is pale grey on white and barely readable.
The processor socket retention frame is a flat silver plate around the pad field with no load lever or hinge on either side, so the socket lacks the mechanism a builder expects.

At the close view the socket retention frame is a plain beveled plate with one small tab at the top and no load lever, hinge or latch hook, which falls short of the lean in test on the board's centerpiece.

The chamfered three fan shroud, the swept blades with hub stickers, the visible fins, the bracket with ports, the single 12V-2x6 socket and the saturated edge bar lighting the fins below it all hold up.
The brushed backplate has its slanted vents, the end cutout over the fins and heat pipes, screws, a sharp wordmark and gold edge fingers, and the hidden bar casts colored light onto the turntable.
It reads as a shorter sibling of the Apex 3X, with a brushed backplate, three slanted vents, a cutout showing fins, pipes and a fan, gold fingers and a sharp APEX 2X mark.

The two power sockets' pin cavities are flat bright white tiles printed on a black face with no recess, metal contact or latch catch, so at this closest view the connectors read as a texture, not as housings.
A thin dark blade sticks out of the far chamfered end cap at the right of the frame with no visible joint or fastener, so it reads as stray geometry, not as a support that is attached to the card.
The backplate has a saturated cyan ring inlay that tints the brushed metal around it, plus slanted vents, a cutout with four heat pipes, gold fingers and a sharp VELTRIN CREST mark.

The static gradient runs from pink at the rear fan through violet at the pump and card to cyan at the three front fans, as pn times 0.66 requires, and it lights the interior, wall and desk mirror with no haze, flare or blackout.

The static Aurora gradient runs from cyan front fans to violet RAM, pump, card bar and rear fan, uniformly dimmed as breathing defines, and the rig still reads against the wall with a soft teal and violet spill on the front panel, board and desk, no clipping and no hard wall shadow.

Every LED shares one green hue as spectrum requires, but the RAM light bars (center, right of the pump) and the card's edge bar above the VELTRIN wordmark wash out to a pale lime close to white, while the fan rings stay deep green, so those diffusers are clipping and not saturated.

The colors change across the rig along the flow axis, from a blue rear fan and cyan pump to a cyan to magenta card bar and magenta front fans, and each zone lights its neighbors, the shroud and the desk with saturated diffusers and no haze or flares.
Every zone shows one violet as shift requires, the diffusers stay saturated, and the violet light falls believably on the board, shroud, wall and desk while the case edges and frame stay readable.

Each zone shows a lit head with a fading tail at its own phase (partial rings on the front and rear fans, a single bright RAM segment, a pink wordmark and cyan tip on the card), and the dimmer frame still separates from the wall without blackout or clipping.

Scattered soft twinkles in mixed Aurora hues sit along the card bar, the RAM and the fan rings over a low base glow, which matches the starlight definition, with no pinpoint flares and the case form still readable.

At load 0 every zone shows a cool saturated blue that fits idle temperatures, and that blue lights the board, shroud, case interior, desk and wall, with no white diffusers and clear separation from the room.

Clearly better than the reference: the glass now shows a framed edge, corner standoffs and reflection streaks, the shroud has a vent field, cable cutouts and a visible drive bay, the lit parts throw color onto the board, wall and desk, and the rig sits on its feet with a clear reflection, with no flares, haze or intersections found.

Clearly better than the reference: the interior is readable from the top radiator's lit rings down to the shroud vents, the pump, two lit Facet sticks, the sleeved runs and the edge-on front fans all match the Night Rig build, and the glass reads through its soft reflection bands without a hard shadow or blackout.

Better than the reference's stretched, moire-prone mesh: the fine round perforation shows the three lit front fans and their mount rails cleanly, the top front shows a power button, the glass edge catches light, and the purple fan light falls on the wall and the desk reflection.

Clearly better than the reference's empty rear: it now shows a ported I/O block with antenna jacks, a grilled rear fan, vented slot covers with the card's video ports, and a supply face with inlet, rocker switch and honeycomb grille, and the interior seen through the glass stays readable and grounded.

Power off and glass off as the bench state requires, the softbox light keeps every part readable with no blackout: radiator print, braided tube, unlit fans, card, board traces, shroud vents and the 3.5 inch bay, and the case sits on its feet with contact shading and a desk reflection.

Clearly better than the reference: the card shows a brushed backplate with vents, an X bracket, screws and a fin cutout, a two color edge bar with a separately lit wordmark, sharp APEX 3X and 12V-2x6 print, and a sleeved cable with real combs, and the 24 pin run bends into its grommet.

Clearly better than the reference's plain cylinder fittings: braided tubes rise from ringed fittings, the X bracket has knurled thumbscrews, the lit cyan ring is saturated rather than clipped and tints the bracket arms, and the KESTRANE TARN 360 LUX print stays sharp.

Clearly better than the reference: the two Facet sticks show a notched light bar and a faceted graphite spreader, the CALYRA FACET DDR5 16 GB label is sharp and matches facet32, the bars tint the board beside them, and the 24 pin sleeves bend smoothly back into the grommet.

Clearly better than the reference's sparse board: it shows traces with sharp silkscreen (KR-SIO, KA-ALC, M.2_3), a CR2032 coin cell, headers, screwed mounting holes, the K chipset plate with its lit accent, and a SATA lead routed into a grommet, and the GPU cable drops cleanly into a rubber-lined shroud cutout.

Better than the reference's oval, stretched perforation: round holes with no moire sit over shaded, twisted blades, a stickered hub and screwed mount rails, and the magenta ring light lights the mesh around each fan with no clipping.

Clearly better than the reference: the orchid sleeves have real braid texture and terminal ends at a modeled 24 pin plug and turn into the grommet, the GPU run curves smoothly from its 12V-2x6 socket, and the braided tubes rise from ringed fittings with nothing passing through anything.

The Thessic supply face is fully modeled with a C14 inlet, an I/O rocker, a honeycomb grille, four screws and sharp THESSIC 850W and 100-240 V print matching the t850 in the build, the case rear has grain and rounded edges, and the case is grounded with a desk reflection.

The chipset accent strip on the right side of the K plate is too bright: its left half turns pale pink-white instead of staying saturated magenta, though the rest of the board has every listed feature, including 4 memory slots, 3 M.2 plates, the reinforced graphics slot, the coin cell and the connector cover strip.

The AC inlet on the rear face (center right) does not read as an inlet: inside the recess there are garbled white shapes instead of a modeled socket with three pins, which weakens an otherwise well finished steel box with a honeycomb grille, a side label and a rocker switch.

The still Aurora gradient runs pink at the rear fan, violet at the pump and memory, and cyan at the front fans as the static formula predicts, every diffuser stays saturated, the light reaches the interior, desk and wall, and the case is grounded with a reflection and no haze or flare.

The frame is caught near the bottom of the breath, so every zone is dimmed evenly in its static Aurora colors as the formula gives at this time, and the case, shroud, board and desk still read clearly with no blackout.

Every zone shows the same saturated yellow-green hue, as the spectrum formula gives at this time, the green spills onto the board, shroud, desk and wall, and no diffuser clips to white (the purple sleeving is the cable colorway, not a light zone).

The Aurora wave is caught mid-travel, blue at the rear fan and pump, a cyan to pink gradient along the card bar, and violet-pink at the front fans, which fits the formula, with saturated diffusers and light cast onto the interior and desk.
Every zone shows one uniform pink-violet blend, as the shift crossfade gives at this time, the color is saturated and not clipped, and it lights the case interior, desk and wall evenly.

The zones sit at a dim floor with short bright heads on the memory bars, the card wordmark, the pump and fan rings, which fits the comet definition, and the dark rig still reads with visible edges and a lit desk.

Scattered soft points of pink, violet and cyan twinkle along the card bar, memory, pump ring and fan rings over a dim base, which matches starlight, and the points are soft diffuser spots rather than hard pinpoint flares.
At load 0 every zone shows the same saturated cold blue that thermal gives for cool parts, the blue lights the interior, desk and wall, and the frame has no clipping, haze or blackout.

Clearly better than the reference: the glass now shows a reflection band and a lit edge, the pump ring, memory, card bar and front fan rings are saturated and light the board, the tray and the desk, the shroud has cutouts and a drive cage, the feet sit on a clean reflection, and I found no haze, flare, blackout or wall shadow.

Clearly better than the reference: three lit top ring fans over the radiator, a lit pump and memory, a board that is readable instead of flat black, a glass reflection, a drive cage in the shroud and a grounded desk reflection, with nothing visibly floating or intersecting.

Clearly better than the reference: the rear panel now carries a ported I/O shield, a perforated rear fan grille, slot covers with a retention bar, card video ports, and a supply face with an inlet, a rocker and a honeycomb, while the interior fans and cable combs light the case and the desk reflection.

Clearly better than the reference: a brushed backplate with a vent row and a cutout, a separately lit wordmark and gradient edge bar that light the shroud lip, a modeled 12V-2x6 plug with braided combed wires, and fins and fan blades visible on the fan side, with sharp text throughout.

Clearly better than the reference: the board now shows traces, an M.2 plate, a coin cell, screw heads, headers, SATA ports with leads curving into a grommet, and a K chipset plate whose accent lights the board beside it, under a card whose lit fin stack is visible, with a rubber-edged cable pass-through below.

The KESTRANE sticker on the middle front fan hub, seen through the mesh at center, reads with reversed letter order and backward glyphs, so the hub print looks mirrored from the front even though the intake face should read correctly.

The supply face reads as powder-coated steel with a hex grille over a fine screen, a modeled three-pin inlet and rocker switch, sharp THESSIC 850W and rating print, and four fixing screws, and the case feet are grounded in the desk reflection.

Every listed board feature is present: the socket with its frame, finned VRM heatsinks, chokes and capacitors, 4 latched memory slots, a reinforced graphics slot plus shorter slots, 3 M.2 plates with diagonal cuts, a K chipset plate, 24-pin and processor power connectors, headers, a coin cell and screwed mounting holes, and both zones (blue cover strip and magenta chipset accent) are saturated and light their surroundings.

A squarer micro ATX version of the Z7 design with 4 memory slots, 2 M.2 plates, a reinforced slot and shorter slots, a K chipset plate, connectors, headers, a coin cell and screws, and only its one chipset accent zone lit in saturated magenta, which lights the board beside it.

The underside is finished, and its pin fields for the memory, slots and 24-pin are mirrored correctly against the front, with a screwed steel socket backplate, brass-ringed mounting holes, a barcode label, small print, and the rear port block standing off the edge.

At close zoom the chokes have rounded edges and sharp R22 and reference print, the capacitors are smooth cylinders with no facets, the traces and pads hold up, and the socket frame has rounded inner corners, corner screws and a dense gold contact field.

The ITX board has no chipset heatsink with the K monogram anywhere on its face (the lower right holds only the coin cell, the memory slots and a header), so it misses a feature 02-PARTS requires on every board and breaks the shared Z7 family design.

The back is finished, with silkscreen, solder dot fields, a screwed brushed steel backplate, four gold-ringed mounting holes in the standard ITX positions and a ported connector block, and the dark board still stands clear of the background.

The diagonal cut lines on the chamfered heatsink block start outside its left edge and hang in the air over the fin stack (top left near 170,110), and the same lines float across the fins at bottom left. The chamfered block corners are razor sharp. The left fin stack reads as pale grey or white metal instead of the satin black that the graphite family calls for.

The chipset accent shows as an unlit black bar on the right edge of the chipset plate, no underglow is visible along the right board edge, and the cover strip is only a faint sliver, so three light zones do not read. The VRM and M.2 heatsinks look like flat matte white plastic, not pale silver aluminum.
A dead black slab runs the full height of the left edge (the board's right edge, x 165 to 180), where the lit underglow strip of this three-zone board should glow onto the edge and turntable.

The socket retention frame is a flat, featureless grey plate with no load lever, no stamped relief and no surface variation. The capacitor tops are plain flat grey discs, and the left fin edge reads as a striped flat texture.

The chipset accent on the K plate is an unlit black bar while the cover strip shows only a faint blue sliver, so the two light zones do not read. The VRM, I/O cover and M.2 heatsinks look like matte white plastic, not pale silver metal.

The back is finished, with silkscreen, solder fields, a barcode label, a brushed steel backplate held by four screws, gold-ringed mounting holes and the ported connector block, all reading clearly against the dark room.

In the top left corner the chokes marked C and A46 overlap each other, and the capacitor near 125,80 sits inside the A97 choke. The socket retention frame is also a flat, featureless grey plate with no lever or stamped relief.

Only one M.2 heatsink plate (marked M.2_2) is visible on the front and none on the back, against a catalog count of two. The I/O cover, VRM and M.2 heatsinks look like matte white plastic, not pale silver aluminum.

The back is finished, with frost silkscreen, solder fields, a barcode label, a brushed steel backplate held by four screws, four gold-ringed ITX mounting holes and a detailed connector block, and the board separates cleanly from the background.

The diagonal cut lines start past the left edge of the chamfered heatsink block and hang in the air over the fin stack (near 170,110 and again at bottom left from 15,650 to 140,790). The chamfered block corner near 190,300 is razor sharp, and the left fin stack breaks into harsh aliased black and white stripes.

The left arc of the pump head ring washes out to near white (around 365 to 380, 490 to 570) instead of holding a saturated color, and the top of the right fan ring goes pastel cyan, although the radiator, white braided tubes, two lit fans and pump otherwise read correctly.

The radiator reads as white, not grey, with rounded end tanks, screws on the side plates and a real tube and fin core, the two lit fans glow through the core in color without clipping, the braided white tubes leave chrome fittings and curve smoothly, and the wordmark on the top rim is legible where the tube does not cover it.

At close range the KESTRANE and TARN 240 FROST print is crisp, the braid weave and ribbed chrome ferrules hold up, the pump rim is beveled, and the cyan to blue ring is saturated and tints the white bezel next to it, so I found nothing on the fail list.

The thick three fan Veltrin shroud has chamfered ends, a brushed face, curved blades with VELTRIN hub stickers, a slotted bracket with ports, a power socket on the top edge and a saturated edge bar and lit wordmark that tint the bevels beside them, and it separates cleanly from the dark turntable.

The steel box has radiused edges and corner screws, a honeycomb grille over a visible fan, a sharp 850W side label with a legible spec table, and a rear face with an inlet, a rocker switch and a perforated vent field, all readable against the dark background.

The colors run as a still gradient front to rear, from teal front fans to blue memory to pink at the rear fan and the card bar, the diffusers stay saturated, and the light falls on the board, the shroud, the wall and the desk reflection without haze or blackout.
The frame keeps the static hues dimmed evenly, as breathing should at a low point of its cycle, while the case edges, the shroud and the desk reflection still read clearly.

Every LED on the fans, pump, memory, card bar and board accents is the same saturated green, which matches spectrum, and the green carries onto the interior, wall and desk with no diffuser clipped to white.

The gradient has moved from where static has it, now blue at the rear fan and pump and magenta at the front fans and card end, so it reads as one wave across the rig, and the colors stay saturated and light their neighbors.
Every zone shows the same violet, as shift should, the diffusers are saturated and not white, and the violet light carries onto the board, the shroud top, the wall and the desk.

Zones are mostly dim with short bright heads and fading tails on the memory, the rear fan ring and the card bar, which matches comet, and the case silhouette, shroud and desk still read against the room.
Single LEDs twinkle as soft colored points over a dim base on the card bar, memory, pump and fan rings, which matches starlight, with no hard pinpoint flares and no blackout of the case.
At load 0 every zone shows a cold saturated blue, which fits the thermal mapping at idle temperatures, and the blue lights the interior, the wall and the desk reflection without clipping.

Clearly better than the reference: braided tubes, lit pump, RAM, card bar and front fans all spill colored light onto the tray, shroud, desk and reflection, the glass shows a soft streak and corner standoffs, and I found no floating, intersecting or blacked out part.

Better than the reference in board texture, cable combs, braided tubes and light spill: the top fan rings light the tray in magenta, the shroud has cutouts with grommets and a brand plate, and the counts match (3 top, 3 front, 1 rear fan, 2 lit sticks).

The round perforated front reads as steel with the three fan blades and rings visible through it and no moire, unlike the smeared mesh in the reference, and the rig is grounded with a colored desk reflection and contact shading.

The hex perforated top shows real panel thickness and front I/O, the backplate shows brushed metal with an X bracket and slanted vents, and the drive label is sharp through the shroud window, so it is clearly richer than the flat reference.

The rear is fully finished where the reference was not: I/O block, a grilled exhaust fan, slot covers with thumbscrews, and a supply with honeycomb, inlet and rocker switch, and the interior lighting stays consistent with the other views.

With the power off and the glass off, the softbox light still shows the case edges, radiator print, board texture, sleeved cables and shroud bays clearly, with nothing melting into black and the rig seated on its reflection.

The card shows a chamfered shroud, fins through the grille, a brushed backplate with an X bracket, slanted vents and an end cutout, a labeled 12V-2x6 socket with a combed sleeved cable, and a two tone edge bar that lights the face, all sharper and more detailed than the reference.

The braided tubes with ringed compression fittings, the X mount with thumbscrews, the pump lead to a header, and the cyan ring lighting the bracket and board are clearly better than the plain tubes in the reference, and the text stays sharp.

In the middle of the frame the two Facet light bars are flat, even violet slabs with no frosted variation, and they throw almost no colored light onto the black CALYRA spreader face right beside them, so the RAM, which is the subject, does not light its neighbors the way the reference's bars do.

The lower board shows traces, an M.2 heatsink, short slots, a printed coin cell, gold antenna jacks, screwed mounting holes, the K chipset plate with a lit accent spilling blue onto the PCB, and SATA leads routed to a grommet, which is far beyond the flat reference.

All six boards share one design: the angled I/O armor with the vertical KORRIN wordmark, M.2 plates with diagonal cuts and a single K monogram plate. The graphite Z7 and frost X9 families scale down cleanly from ATX to ITX, and nothing reads as another brand or a real maker's signature board.

The air towers share dimpled top plates, nickel pipes, dense black fin stacks and wire clips, the Tarn liquid coolers share the round lit-ring pump with the capital wordmark and braided tubes, and the three fans share the frame, blade shape and capital hub mark. The slate fan's pale grey hub is the one slightly odd note, but no part reads as Lumenfold or as a real maker's signature product.

Petal and Frame share the soft rounded pillow frame with round corner holes, broad translucent blades and the mixed-case Lumenfold hub mark. This sets them clearly apart from Kestrane's squarer chamfered frames with corner pads and capital wordmark, even though Frame comes in graphite.

Every kit carries the same wide-spaced CALYRA wordmark and label layout. The three Facet kits differ only by label and stick count, Mono is the plain low satin black sibling, and Crown repeats the Facet angled facet panels in white under a lit crown. The faceted light-bar look stays within the genre and does not copy a real kit.

All four cards share the chamfered tail and chamfered shroud perimeter, the same fan rotor with the VELTRIN hub mark, and the spaced wordmark on the edge facing the glass. Mini and Crest read as the short and flagship siblings, and the chamfered silhouette keeps every card apart from the Dravik slabs.

The slab silhouettes and block DRAVIK wordmark tie the four cards together. Arrow, Flint and Vault share one label system: the PELLAM wordmark over a large bold name and capacity, technical small print with a barcode or code block, and a colored corner tab per drive type (violet, teal, amber). They read as one plain, honest family with no real maker's label styling.

Ember 8 (square, green substrate, Cindervane bar mark) and Tidal 16 (longer, dark substrate, notched heat spreader corner, Hadron Bay wave mark) cannot be mistaken for each other. Vitrine and Atrium hang together as a family with their slim black or white frames and large glass, but in the top left tile the Vitrine has the same box proportions, perforated front and top, rear fan grille, tray cutouts and shroud block as the Skarn Vent, so without its wordmark it could pass for a Skarn, and both cases carry the same chrome corner glass caps that the Skarn and Paleforge cases use, which goes against the hidden fasteners the brand is defined by.

Vent and Bulwark match each other, but in both top tiles the Vent reads as the Mirevale Vitrine with a bigger wordmark, the SKARN mark on every shroud is a plain bold sans with no stencil breaks, the front is flat with no visible bow, and there are no exposed hex screws or chamfered corners anywhere on the sheet, with only a faint ribbed area at the top rear and the same chrome glass corner caps as the other brands, so nothing on the sheet clearly marks it as an industrial airflow brand.

The two cases share no clear Paleforge feature: the Cub in the top tiles has a thick rounded shell with large chrome glass standoffs, while the Gantry in the bottom tiles is a thin, square, enclosed looking frame whose glass sits flush with barely visible corner fixings instead of standing on pillars, no thick plate edges or bead blasted texture shows on either case, the white Cub looks like glossy powder coat, and the black Gantry in the bottom right looks like a Mirevale piece with large glass and a slim black frame.

The blue to violet gradient is saturated on the pump ring, rear fan ring, memory bars and card edge bar, it lights the board, shroud and interior walls, it washes the wall and desk to match, the case is seated with a reflection, and no haze, flare or blackout shows.

The diffusers inside are orange and red, but the wall behind the rig and the desk around its base stay violet, so the rig's warm light does not reach the room the way the build's average color should.
The memory light bars at the top center and the rear fan ring at the upper left read as nearly white with almost no cyan left at the diffuser, while the pump ring beside them keeps its color.

Every LED shows the same yellow green as the spectrum effect requires, the diffusers stay saturated, and the color spills onto the board, the shroud, the interior front wall, the desk and the wall with no flare or clipping.
The memory light bars at the top center wash out to a pale lilac that is close to white, so the color does not hold at the diffuser even though the pump and fan rings next to them stay deep magenta.

The green from the rings, memory bars and card bar stays inside the case, and the wall behind the rig and the desk around its base stay blue violet with no green wash, unlike the spectrum shot where the room picks up the rig's color.
The star highlights on the card edge bar at the left of the VELTRIN wordmark and on the tops of the memory bars bloom into colorless white blobs instead of keeping a saturated color at the diffuser.
At load 0 the thermal effect gives a cool, saturated blue on every zone, the light falls on the board, the shroud, the desk and the wall, and the frame has no haze, clipping or flare.

All diffusers are dark as brightness 0 requires, and the softboxes still show the case silhouette against the violet wall pool, with the parts inside reading as dark grey with edge highlights and the desk and its reflection visible, so X15 does not apply.

The card's edge bar and wordmark are dark, the memory runs its own saturated red profile that lights the board area beside it, and every other zone keeps the main gradient, so each override applies to exactly its target.

Dravik cards: square flat shroud, straight edge light, square fan rings; unlike Veltrin.

This is not clearly better than the reference: a grey veil covers the lower half over the shroud and lower glass, the board to the right of the memory breaks up into blue speckle noise instead of readable traces, and the three front fans behind the perforated front are faint pink outlines where the reference shows them glowing.

The board area right of the memory and behind the pump has a pale blue-white smeared blotch that reads like a stain or texture artifact, and the white interior picks up a flat blue-grey cast, so the frost finish does not read cleanly as white powder coat in the upper chamber.

The interior is so dark that the board melts into black-blue speckle, the twin cooler's two towers read as flat black slabs with dot patterns and show no fin edges, and the three 140 mm front fans cannot be seen through the glass along the front of the interior.

The white board is covered in grey grimy blotches that read as dirt instead of a clean circuit surface, and only one liquid cooling tube runs across the top to the front where two braided tubes should show.

The pump cap and the rear fan ring are washed out to near white pastel pink instead of saturated color, and the blue-white sleeved graphics power loops bunch into a tangled inverted U against the slanted grey plate above the card, so they do not clearly clear it.

The board and cooler area under the top of the frame is murky and nearly black so its form is hard to read, the board right of the memory breaks into blue speckle noise, and the silver top strip and right panel make the open frame read as an enclosed case.
